NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be subsequently ap­
pointed by me, to investigate the said 
dispute.

No member of the said board 
shall be pecuniarily or otherwise inter­
ested in any organization of railway em­
ployees or any carrier.

The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.

As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the River Terminal Railway 
Company or its employees in the con­
ditions out of which the dispute arose.

Each member of the board shall ,  re­
ceive compensation at the rate of sev­
enty-five dollars a day for each day that 
he is actually engaged in the perform­
ance of his duties or in travel in con­
nection therewith.

The compensation and expenses of the 
board and its employees shall be paid 
out of the appropriation “Arbitration 
and Emergency Boards, National Media«'
tion Board, 1945” on the presentation of 
itemized vouchers properly approved by 
the chairman of the board.

Section 1. Establishment of the Award. In order to encourage love of country, 
service to the people of the United States, and support for our Armed 
Forces, and in order to recognize the unique and lifelong service of Bob 
Hope to the United States Armed Forces and to the Nation through his 
unwavering patriotism and dedication to maintaining the morale of the 
troops he entertained for nearly six decades, and on the occasion of his 
100th birthday, there is hereby established the Bob Hope American Patriot 
Award (Award). 
Sec. 2. Granting and Presentation of the Award.
(a) The Award may be granted by the President, in his sole discretion, 
to any civilian individual who has demonstrated extraordinary love of coun-
try and devotion to the personnel of the United States Armed Forces, in 
the form of true patriotism. The Award may also be granted by the President 
to an organization that meets the same criteria. 
(b) Other than in exceptional circumstances, no more than one Award 
may be granted in any given year. 
(c) The presentation of the Award may take place at any time during 
the year. 
(d) Subject to the provisions of this order, the Award may be conferred 
posthumously.

operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Section 1. Policy. It is the policy of the Federal Government to ensure 
that each executive branch agency can perform its essential functions and 
remain an effectively functioning part of the Federal Government under 
all conditions. Accordingly, each agency shall take all appropriate actions 
to establish, maintain, and, as necessary, revise an order of succession, 
or to propose presidential action to establish or revise an order of succession. 
Sec. 2. Definitions. As used in this order: 
(a) ‘‘agency’’ means: 
(i) an executive agency as defined in section 105 of title 5, United 
States Code, other than the Government Accountability Office; and 
(ii) the United States Postal Service and the Postal Regulatory Com-
mission; and 
(b) ‘‘order of succession’’ means a list of officials by position who shall 
act as and perform the functions and duties of the office of the head 
of the agency in the event that the office-holder has died, resigned, or 
otherwise become unable to perform the functions and duties of the office. 
‘‘Order of succession’’ does not include any order, rule, memorandum, 
or other document delegating or partially delegating the authority of an 
office. 
Sec. 3. Orders of Succession Requiring Presidential Action.  
(a) Each agency for which presidential action is required to establish 
an order of succession shall draft a proposed order of succession if no 
such order exists and, not later than 30 days from the date of this order, 
send such proposed draft order to the Counsel to the President for review 
and comment. 
(b) Each agency described in subsection 3(a) of this order shall send 
any proposed updates or revisions to the agency’s order of succession 
to the Counsel to the President for review and comment. 
(c) Upon completion of the requirements set forth by subsections (a) 
or (b) of this section with respect to a proposed order, the agency shall 
submit the proposed order to the Office of Management and Budget in 
accordance with Executive Order 11030, as amended. 
Sec. 4. Orders of Succession Not Requiring Presidential Action. (a) Each 
agency for which presidential action is not required to establish an order 
of succession because of the agency’s existing legal authority shall establish 
and maintain such order in accordance with applicable law and any applica-
ble guidance issued by the President or the Secretary of Homeland Security, 
including the laws and guidance regarding continuity plans and programs 
for the executive branch. 
(b) Each agency described in subsection 4(a) of this order shall update 
and revise its order of succession as necessary. Before implementing any 
revisions to its order of succession, such agency shall send the proposed 
revisions to the Counsel to the President for review and comment. 
(c) Not later than 30 days from the date of this order, and not later 
than 7 days from the issuance date of any subsequent final revision

Sec. 5. General Provisions. (a) Nothing in this order shall be construed 
to impair or otherwise affect: 
(i) authority granted by law to a department, agency, or the head 
thereof; or 
(ii) functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget 
relating to budget, administrative, or legislative proposals. 
(b) Nothing in this order shall be construed to delegate the President’s 
authority under the Federal Vacancies Reform Act of 1998, 5 U.S.C. 3345 
et seq ., to designate individuals to perform the functions and duties of 
a vacant office temporarily in an acting capacity. 
(c) This order shall be implemented in a manner consistent with applicable 
law and subject to the availability of appropriations. 
(d) This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or 
benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity, by 
any party against the United States, its agencies, instrumentalities, or 
entities, its officers, employees, or agents, or any other person.

operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Section 1. Establishment. The Administrator of the Small Business Adminis-
tration (Administrator) shall establish within the Small Business Administra-
tion an Interagency Task Force on Veterans Small Business Development 
(Task Force). 
Sec. 2. Membership. The Administrator shall serve as Chair of the Task 
Force and shall direct its work. Other members shall consist of: 
(a) a senior level representative, designated by the head of the respective 
department or agency, from each of the following: 
(i) the Department of the Treasury; 
(ii) the Department of Defense; 
(iii) the Department of Labor; 
(iv) the Department of Veterans Affairs; 
(v) the Office of Management and Budget; 
(vi) the Small Business Administration (in addition to the Administrator); 
and 
(vii) the General Services Administration; and 
(b) four representatives from a veterans’ service or military organization 
or association, who shall be appointed by the Administrator. 
Sec. 3. Functions. Consistent with the Act and other applicable law, the 
Task Force shall: 
(a) consult regularly with veterans service and military organizations in 
performing the duties of the Task Force; 
(b) coordinate administrative and regulatory activities and develop pro-
posals relating to: 
(i) improving capital access and capacity of small business concerns owned 
and controlled by veterans and service-disabled veterans through loans, 
surety bonding, and franchising; 
(ii) ensuring achievement of the pre-established Federal contracting goals 
for small business concerns owned and controlled by veterans and service- 
disabled veterans through expanded mentor-prote´ge´ assistance and match-
ing such small business concerns with contracting opportunities; 
(iii) increasing the integrity of certifications of status as a small business 
concern owned and controlled by a veteran or service-disabled veteran; 
(iv) reducing paperwork and administrative burdens on veterans in access-
ing business development and entrepreneurship opportunities;

(v) increasing and improving training and counseling services provided 
to small business concerns owned and controlled by veterans; and 
(vi) making other improvements relating to the support for veterans busi-
ness development by the Federal Government; and 
(c) not later than 1 year after its first meeting and annually thereafter, 
forward to the President a report on the performance of its functions, includ-
ing any proposals developed pursuant to subsection (b) of this section. 
Sec. 4. General Provisions . (a) The Small Business Administration shall 
provide funding and administrative support for the Task Force to the extent 
permitted by law and within existing appropriations. 
(b) Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise effect: 
(i) authority granted by law to an executive department, agency, or the 
head thereof; and 
(ii) functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget 
relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals. 
(c) Insofar as the Federal Advisory Committee Act, as amended (5 U.S.C. 
App.) (FACA), may apply to the Task Force, any functions of the President 
under the FACA, except for those in section 6 of the FACA, shall be 
performed by the Administrator in accordance with guidelines issued by 
the Administrator of General Services. 
(d) This order is not intended to and does not create any right or benefit, 
substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party 
against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, 
employees, or agents, or any other person.

Its five operative clauses contain no fixed end date, event-triggered cessation, delegation transfer or savings qualification. The exact retained official Federal Register page was visually compared to its complete text and signature; its byte hash matches both stage21 custody and full_run source metadata. The current U.S.Code note reproduces the same five clauses, corroborating continuation throughOctober9 rather than supplying a new source of authority. To assess the October14cutoff, the researcher reviewed the saved OFR catalog current to that cutoff, all numeric13306hits and unparsed-note hits, and the bounded eCFR and later-order-text scan described below. Two other catalog numericmatches are page/document-number collisions; no adverse disposition or amendment is identified for this order. This supports continued operation of the original authority within those bounded searches. No judicial or statutory contrarylead is identified in the saved inputs; unnamed statutory displacement and uncatalogued decisions are limitations of the bounded search, not invented findings of absence. No human certification or GPOpublished fixity confirmation is asserted.

unresolved_material_gaps: Clause EO:11262#sec1-item4-level-IV: the actual termination date of the President's Commission on Law Enforcement and Administration of Justice is not in held sources (EO 11236: terminate not later than 90 days after the final report). The clause ended on that date or, at the latest, on 1968-04-29 (EO 11409 item 1(b)). Needs the commission's report and termination record.
research_rationale: EO 11262 adds three items to EO 11248: in level IV, (4) Executive Secretary of the President's Commission on Law Enforcement and Administration of Justice; in level V, (4) Director, Bureau of Outdoor Recreation and (5) Assistant to the Secretary of Defense (Legislative Affairs). No later amender deleted the two level V items (traced item by item through EO 11699); they ended with EO 11708 sec. 3 on March 23, 1973. EO 11409 item 1(b) formally deleted the level IV item on April 29, 1968. That position, however, belonged to a temporary commission: EO 11236 (held, 30 FR 9349) required the commission to report within 18 months and to terminate not later than 90 days after its report. The placement therefore probably lost its object before the 1968 deletion. Deadlines cannot fix the actual date, so that clause's first_end stays open. The whole-order end is unaffected because the two level V items ran to 1973-03-23. research_rationale: EO 11489 replaces level IV item (1) of EO 11248, the Special Assistant to the Secretary (for Enforcement), Treasury, with the Special Assistant to the Secretary (Congressional Relations), Treasury. Removing the old item was completed on October 27, 1969. The inserted item was in turn deleted by EO 11699 (38 FR 2323; signed January 22, 1973; no other effective date), which put the Assistant to the Secretary for Legislative Affairs in its place. This order's placement therefore ended on 1973-01-22. EO 11708 sec. 1(4) later places the Congressional Relations position again by its own authority, a new placement that is not this order's. The OFR catalog shows no disposition for EO 11489; the Codification's 'Revoked by EO 11708' is the later formal revocation, recorded as a post-end event. Family method: the researcher read the saved official Federal Register OCR text layers (heading to FR Doc line) of this order, of EO 11248 and of all 40 orders that the OFR disposition notes and the 1989 Codification list as amending it, plus EO 11708, 11715, 11736 and 11768, and traced every item of EO 11248 sections 1 and 2 through each addition, deletion, word substitution and renumbering. EO 11708 sec. 3 (signed and filed March 23, 1973; no other effective date) revokes EO 11248 as amended, except for the eight positions listed in its section 2; none of them is a position whose placement this order's text still supplied. Where a later amender deletes an item and inserts another in its place, the earlier item's placement ends on that amender's effective date; the series' separate 'substituting for the words' formula is treated as a retitling that continues the item. Pure deletions, renumberings and effective-date provisions are one-time edits completed when the order took effect. The 5 U.S.C. 5315-5316 amendment notes for 1964-1973 record no statutory placement of the positions concerned. Abolition of a position by unpublished departmental action is outside the held sources and is a limitation of this bounded search. Page images were not viewed; quotations are exact from the saved OCR, including its recognition errors. No human certification is asserted.

savings_residuals.reason: Neither EO 12332 nor the revoking EO 12534 contains a savings clause, and EO 12534 sec. 3 states that the committees it lists had already terminated. Members served without compensation (travel expenses only) and the Treasury support and FACA delegation in sections 3(c) and 4(a) applied only to the Committee. No rights, entitlements, property, delegations or functions outside the body itself were created, so nothing survives its termination; reimbursements and support given while it existed are completed transactions, not continuing effects. research_rationale: EO 12332 (Nov. 10, 1981; 46 FR 55913) established the National Productivity Advisory Committee under FACA. All twelve operative subsections (secs. 1(a)-4(b)) concern that Committee: composition, advisory functions, agency information, unpaid service, Treasury support, the Executive Secretary, the FACA delegation to the Secretary of the Treasury, and the sec. 4(b) sunset of December 31, 1982 'unless sooner extended'. EO 12399 sec. 1(l), effective December 31, 1982 (sec. 6), continued the Committee 'until September 30, 1984'. The next continuance order, EO 12489 (Sept. 28, 1984), lists other committees but not this one, and no other held order, OFR catalog note or the 1989 Codification ('Continued by EO 12399'; 'Revoked by EO 12534') shows a further extension. The Committee therefore terminated on September 30, 1984, which is the first end of every clause and the whole-order end. EO 12534 sec. 3(f), effective September 30, 1985 (sec. 5), revoked the order as one 'which established committees that have terminated'; it is a later event, not the first end. The draft's FULL_AND_PARTIAL_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT is resolved by reading EO 12534 sec. 3, which revokes each listed order as a whole; the 'partial' reading came only from the OFR catalog's acting-order phrasing 'Revokes advisory committees established by'. Quotations are verbatim from the saved govinfo OCR text of the Federal Register issue, which is letter-spaced on these pages; the pdfplumber recheck text has the same wording. The draft's page range (PDF pages 11-17) ran into later documents and is corrected to pages 11-12. No human certification is asserted.

research_rationale: EO 12369 (June 30, 1982; 47 FR 28899) established the Executive Committee of the President's Private Sector Survey on Cost Control under FACA. Its twelve operative subsections (secs. 1(a)-4(b), with the five recommendation areas inside sec. 2(c)) all concern that Committee. Section 4(b) set termination on December 31, 1982 'unless sooner extended'. Each term was extended before it lapsed: EO 12398 (Dec. 31, 1982; also raised membership to 170) to June 30, 1983; EO 12429 (June 28, 1983) to October 30, 1983; EO 12447 (Oct. 27, 1983) to December 31, 1983; EO 12455 (Dec. 29, 1983) to January 31, 1984. None of these states a separate effective date, so each took effect on signing. No later extension appears in the held order texts, the OFR catalog notes or the 1989 Codification (amendments listed are exactly these four), and the Committee is not in the continuance orders EO 12399 or EO 12489. The Committee and every clause therefore ended on January 31, 1984 (whole-order end). EO 12534 sec. 3(b), effective September 30, 1985, is a later cleanup revocation. The draft's FULL_AND_PARTIAL_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT is resolved by reading EO 12534 sec. 3, which revokes each listed order as a whole; the 'partial' reading came only from the OFR catalog's acting-order phrasing 'Revokes advisory committees established by'. The last words of sec. 3(d) continue on the next page after the running head; that continuation is quoted in the clause's original_source. No human certification is asserted.

research_rationale: EO 12400 (Jan. 3, 1983; 48 FR 381) established the President's Commission on Strategic Forces under FACA; its nine operative subsections all concern that Commission. Original sec. 4(b) ended it 30 days after its report (due February 18, 1983). EO 12406 (Feb. 18, 1983) moved the report deadline to April 15, 1983 and the end to 60 days after reporting; EO 12424 (June 10, 1983), which records the report as 'dated April 11, 1983', gave the Commission a new review mandate (sec. 2(a)), a report deadline of December 15, 1983 (sec. 2(b)) and a fixed end: 'terminate on January 3, 1984, unless sooner extended' (sec. 4(b)). EO 12424 was signed on the 60th day after April 11, 1983, so the Commission did not lapse before the extension (if the report reached the President later than its date, the margin is larger). No later extension appears in the held order texts, the OFR catalog notes or the 1989 Codification (amendments listed: EOs 12406, 12424), and the Commission is not in continuance order EO 12489. savings_residuals.reason: Neither EO 12412 nor the revoking EO 12534 contains a savings clause, and EO 12534 sec. 3 states that the committees it lists had already terminated. Members received no compensation (travel expenses only) and the Peace Corps support and FACA delegation in secs. 3(c) and 4(a) applied only to the Council; the later Presidential Advisory Council on the Peace Corps was a new body created by EO 12468, not a continuation of this one. No rights, entitlements, property, delegations or functions outside the body itself were created, so nothing survives its termination; reimbursements and support given while it existed are completed transactions, not continuing effects. research_rationale: EO 12412 (Mar. 29, 1983; 48 FR 13393) established the Peace Corps Advisory Council under FACA; its nine operative subsections all concern that Council (composition, advice, annual report, agency information, unpaid service, Peace Corps support, FACA delegation). Section 4(b) reads 'The Council shall terminate on December 31, 1983, unless sooner extended.' No amending or extending order exists: the 1989 Codification lists no amendments, the OFR catalog notes record only the EO 12534 revocation, the saved later order texts cite it only in EO 12534, and the Council is not in continuance order EO 12489. The Council and every clause therefore ended on December 31, 1983 by the order's own term (whole-order end). EO 12468 (Mar. 22, 1984) later created a different body, the Presidential Advisory Council on the Peace Corps. EO 12534 sec. 3(g), effective September 30, 1985, is a later cleanup revocation. The draft's FULL_AND_PARTIAL_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT is resolved by reading EO 12534 sec. 3, which revokes each listed order as a whole; the 'partial' reading came only from the OFR catalog's acting-order phrasing 'Revokes advisory committees established by'. Section 3(a) says 'Com m ission' in the printed text; the quotation keeps it. No human certification is asserted.

research_rationale: EO 9451 (June 20, 1944; 9 FR 6905) has one operative provision: paragraph 2 of EO 9243 (priority classifications among departments and agencies for the transfer and release of Federal personnel) 'is hereby revoked, effective as of July 1, 1944.' Its only effect is that partial revocation of EO 9243. EO 9695 para. 1 (Feb. 8, 1946; 11 FR 1559) revoked EO 9243 as a whole; it states no effective date, so it took effect on signing. Following the 1989 Codification's treatment of this order ('Amended EO 9243'; 'Revoked by EO 9695'), the amendment's lifecycle ends with the revocation of the order it amended, on February 8, 1946; the revocation of para. 2 itself had already taken effect on July 1, 1944 and was never reversed (EO 9695 revives nothing). No other order touched EO 9243 para. 2 in between (OFR catalog and saved later texts show no citation of this order). A reviewer who instead treats a revoking provision as spent on its own effective date would date the end July 1, 1944; this claim adopts the Codification convention used for amending orders. No human certification is asserted.

Sec. 4(b) ends the Commission thirty days after it submitted its report (due by January 20, 1983 under sec. 2(b) as amended by EO 12402). research_rationale: EO 12335 (Dec. 16, 1981; 46 FR 61633) established the National Commission on Social Security Reform under FACA; its nine operative subsections all concern the Commission. The order has no fixed termination date, so the Commission's end depends on the actual submission date, which no held source records. Every clause is terminated (EO 12534 sec. 3 lists the order among those whose committees had terminated, and revoked it effective September 30, 1985), but the first-end date is left open rather than inferred from the deadline. research_rationale: EO 12401 (Jan. 14, 1983; 48 FR 2309) established the Presidential Commission on Indian Reservation Economies under FACA; its fourteen operative subsections all concern the Commission. Original sec. 4(b) ended it 60 days after its final report or on December 31, 1983, whichever came earlier (report due by Sept. 30, 1983 under sec. 2(d)). EO 12442 (Sept. 21, 1983) moved the report deadline to November 30, 1984 and replaced sec. 4(b) with termination '30 days after it transmits its final report'. Whether the Commission had already lapsed under the original terms before September 21, 1983, and when it transmitted its final report, are not shown by any held source; so every clause is terminated (EO 12534 sec. 3(n) lists it among terminated committees) but the first-end date is left open. The draft's FULL_AND_PARTIAL_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT is resolved by reading EO 12534 sec. 3, which revokes each listed order as a whole; the 'partial' reading came only from the OFR catalog's acting-order phrasing 'Revokes advisory committees established by'. The end of sec. 3(b) continues on the next page and is quoted in its original_source. No human certification is asserted.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 11408 contains no savings, transition or continuation clause. Its section 1 revoked Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873 (the dual federal-state office-holding prohibition) itself, and section 2 revoked every prior order insofar as it interpreted or amended that order. This order's only operative content is an amendment of (an exception to) that 1873 order, so once the prohibition itself was revoked nothing remained for the exception to operate on, and no office, fund, property, entitlement or enforceable right was created by the order that could survive; office-holding done under the permission before 1968 was lawful when done and is a completed historical fact, not a continuing effect.

research_rationale: Executive Order 7636 (official Federal Register text, 2 FR 1259, PDF pages 1-1, read in the saved OCR text layer of the govinfo issue PDF: heading, enacting clause, operative text and signature/filing line are all present) permits state, county or municipal officers elected by grazing-district voters and appointed by the Secretary of the Interior to serve as district advisors under the Taylor Grazing Act of June 28, 1934. Its whole operative content is an amendment of Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873, as amended (the 1989 OFR disposition table: 'Amended EO 9'; 'Revoked by EO 11408'). EO 11408 of April 25, 1968 (33 FR 6459, saved official text read in full) revoked EO 9 itself in section 1 and in section 2 revoked 'All prior Executive orders insofar as they interpret or amend Executive Order No. 9'; EO 11408 section 2 names it expressly in its list of revoked amendatory orders. Because the order consists only of that amendment, 'insofar as' reaches all of it, which is also why the OFR catalog's '(in part)' qualifier on some of these notes does not leave any part in force. EO 11408 states no effective date, so the revocation took effect on signing, 1968-04-25. No earlier end was found: the order has no expiry, condition or temporary term, the OFR catalog and the saved-text corpus show no earlier amendment or revocation, and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches show no current citation. Each clause therefore first ended on 1968-04-25 and that is the whole-order end. OCR quotations keep the scan's recognition errors (and soft hyphens) exactly as held; they have not been compared with page images.

research_rationale: EO 10358 of June 9, 1952 (official text 17 FR 5269, saved OCR text layer of the govinfo issue PDF read in full from heading to signature and filing line) sets holiday-observance rules for executive agencies: application (s.1), definitions of holiday and workday (s.2), closing of offices on the Monday after a Sunday holiday (s.3), next-workday and in-lieu rules for employees (ss.4-6), pay-and-leave treatment (s.7), and an effective date sixty days after signing with supersession of EO 9636 (s.8). EO 11226 (May 27, 1965, 30 FR 7213) rewrote section 7 and added a section 9 for employees on uncommon tours of duty, effective on issuance; EO 11272 (February 23, 1966, 31 FR 3111) rewrote section 1 and added a section 10 excluding the postal field service from sections 4-7 and 9, effective on issuance. These amendments modified but did not end any original clause (each rewritten clause kept its original rule), so they are recorded as later events, not first ends. EO 11582 of February 11, 1971 (36 FR 2957, read in full) section 8 revokes EO 10358 and the amendatory EOs 11226 and 11272, and section 9 makes the order 'effective as of January 1, 1971', so the revocation is effective 1971-01-01 (the same day the Monday-holiday statute moved several of the dates listed in section 2(a); nothing ended any clause earlier). The order has no expiry or condition. The eCFR conflict lead (7 CFR 800.0 still mentions 'Executive Order 10358, as amended' when explaining weekend holiday observance) was read: it is a stale descriptive cross-reference in a grain-inspection definition and cannot keep a revoked order operating; the operative rules are 5 U.S.C. 6103 and EO 11582, so the lead is resolved and does not contradict the NO status. Section 8 is inventoried in two quoted parts because the OCR fuses the footnote marker to the superseded order's number (the number would not be a valid order number as printed); the omitted token is the number of EO 9636, identified by its date and title. All clauses first ended 1971-01-01, which is the whole-order end. OCR quotations are exact copies of the held text and have not been compared with page images.

Those transfers are accrued results; the continuing authority after January 7, 1947 is EO 9818's, not EO 9789's. Paragraph 7's amendment of EO 9142 is likewise restated in EO 9818 paragraph 7.

research_rationale: EO 9789 of October 14, 1946 (official text 11 FR 11981, saved OCR text layer of the govinfo issue PDF read in full from heading to signature and filing line, F.R. Doc. 46-18658) establishes the Philippine Alien Property Administration and defines its functions in nine paragraphs; it takes effect October 14, 1946 (paragraph 9). The text is printed across columns interrupted by the issue's contents and codification guide, so paragraph 2 is inventoried in two quoted parts (before and after the interruption); no other text belongs to the order. EO 9788, signed the same day (F.R. Doc. 46-18657) and effective October 15, 1946, terminated the Office of Alien Property Custodian and moved its functions to the Attorney General; it is recorded as a later event on the clauses that direct the Custodian to act, because it changed who performed them without ending them. EO 9818 of January 7, 1947 (12 FR 133, read in full) re-issues the order with changes and in paragraph 9 provides 'This order supersedes Executive Order ... of October 14, 1946, entitled "Establishing the Philippine Alien Property Administration and defining its functions."' (OCR prints the number '928.9'; the date and title identify EO 9789). EO 9818 states no effective date, so the supersession took effect on signing, 1947-01-07. This resolves the draft's undated-ending conflict. No earlier end was found: EO 9789 has no expiry or condition, no evidence shows any directive was fully performed before supersession, and the OFR catalog, the saved-text corpus and the U.S. Code/eCFR hits (historical notes) show no other event. All clauses first ended 1947-01-07, the whole-order end. OCR quotations are exact copies of the held text, not compared with page images.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 10697 contains no savings or transition clause. It prescribes a complete new Tariff of Fees and its own collection rules (sections 1-6), effective March 1, 1957, and revokes the earlier tariff orders to the extent not already revoked or superseded. Fees charged under the earlier tariff were completed transactions; the order created no fund, office, property or vested right that survived. The sub-items this order wrote for the Nationality Act of 1940 had already been replaced in 1953 with effect as of December 24, 1952, so nothing of them reached 1957.

research_rationale: EO 9767 of August 9, 1946 (official text 11 FR 8710, saved OCR text layer of the govinfo issue PDF read in full from heading to signature and filing line; its last line is printed on the next page after a fragment of another document, so paragraph (d) is inventoried in two parts) amends the Tariff of United States Foreign Service Fees (section V-15 of the Foreign Service Regulations, EO 7968 as amended): (a) rewrites the last sub-item of Item 6 (certified copy of a repatriation form under the Nationality Act of 1940), (b) revokes the first exception under Item 24, (c) and (d) rewrite the second and third exceptions under Item 24 (no-fee oaths of allegiance under the 1940 Act). EO 10473 of July 22, 1953 (18 FR 4351, read in full) section 4(b)(3) amends 'The last item' of Item 6 to the Immigration and Nationality Act repatriation form, section 4(d)(1) revokes 'The first item under the word Exceptions' of Item 24 and section 4(d)(3) amends 'The last item appearing under the word Exceptions', each 'effective as of December 24, 1952'. No amendatory order intervened between 1946 and 1953 (EO 10697 section 7 lists the whole chain: 7968, 8297, 9303, 9407, 9507, 9591, 9767, 10473, 10639), so after EO 9767 revoked the first exception its (c) item was the first item and its (d) item the last; the successor texts match them item for item (same subjects, with the 1952 Act substituted). Those three clauses therefore first ended 1952-12-24. The opening amending clause and the revocation in (b) stayed in force until EO 10697 of February 6, 1957 (22 FR 777, read in full), which prescribed a new Tariff of Fees and in section 7 revoked EO 9767 'To the extent that they have not heretofore been revoked or superseded', effective March 1, 1957 (section 8). Whole-order end: 1957-03-01. OCR quotations are exact copies of the held text, not compared with page images.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 10697 contains no savings or transition clause. It prescribes a complete new Tariff of Fees and its own collection rules (sections 1-6), effective March 1, 1957, and revokes the earlier tariff orders to the extent not already revoked or superseded. Fees charged under the earlier tariff were completed transactions; the order created no fund, office, property or vested right that survived. EO 10697 sections 2-5 restate the collection rules this order had written into section V-15 as EO 10697's own provisions; section 1's revocation of section V-14 was a completed disposition that nothing reversed.

research_rationale: EO 10473 of July 22, 1953 (official text 18 FR 4351-4352, saved OCR text layer read in full; the order continues from PDF page 1 to page 2 after the issue's contents, with no text lost between paragraph 4(c) and 4(d)) amends the Foreign Service Regulations (EO 7968): revokes section V-14 (s.1), rewrites paragraphs (a)-(b) of section V-15 (s.2), corrects the citation in V-15(d) (s.3) and amends Tariff Items 3, 6, 7, 24 and 45 (s.4), with an inconsistency clause (s.5) and effect on publication except where stated (s.6). EO 10639 of October 10, 1955 (20 FR 7717, read in full) deleted Tariff Items 1-5, effective ten days after publication (published October 14, 1955), which ended section 4(a)'s exception to Item 3 on 1955-10-24. Every other clause stayed in force until EO 10697 of February 6, 1957 (22 FR 777, read in full) prescribed a complete new Tariff of Fees and collection rules and in section 7 revoked EO 10473 'To the extent that they have not heretofore been revoked or superseded', effective March 1, 1957 (section 8). No other event was found in the OFR catalog, the saved-text corpus or the U.S. Code/eCFR searches. Whole-order end: 1957-03-01. OCR quotations (including garbled fee figures such as 'i. oo') are exact copies of the held text, not compared with page images.

research_rationale: EO 9591 of July 21, 1945 (official text 10 FR 9205, saved OCR text layer of the govinfo issue PDF read in full). The OCR interleaves columns: the order's heading, enacting clause and paragraphs 1-2 run continuously, then text of EO 9592 and a Civil Service Commission rule intervene before the signature block 'July 21,1945' with F.R. Doc. 45-13508 (EO 9592 carries 45-13509 and its own signature), so the order consists of paragraphs 1 and 2 only. Paragraph 1's opening words are quoted up to the parenthetical citation because the OCR fuses footnote markers to the cited order numbers there (the fused figures are not valid order numbers); the parenthetical cites EO 7968 as amended by EOs 8297, 9303, 9407 and 9507. Paragraph 1 amends Tariff Items 6, 8 and 34; paragraph 2 amends section V-23 of the Foreign Service Regulations. EO 9767 (1946) and EO 10473 (1953) changed other sub-items of Item 6 but not the eighth heading 'Issue of card or certificate of identity and registration' (EO 10473 inserts a new item immediately below it, so it still stood in 1953), Item 8 or Item 34; EO 10639 (1955) deleted only Items 1-5. EO 10697 (22 FR 777, read in full) prescribed a complete new Tariff effective March 1, 1957 and in section 7 revoked EO 9591, so paragraph 1's clauses first ended 1957-03-01. Paragraph 2 is left open (see the gap): its host section V-23 may have lapsed earlier. This is a partial claim: original text, clause inventory, savings and later-source search are asserted; the ending is not.

Section 1. Statutory Pay Systems.  Pursuant to the provisions of subchapter I of  
Chapter 53 of Title 5 of the United States Code, the rates of basic pay and salaries are  
adjusted, as set forth at the schedules attached hereto and made a part hereof, for the  
following statutory pay systems:
(a) The General Schedule (5 U.S.C. 5 3 32(a)) at Schedule 1;
(b) the schedules for the Foreign Service (22 U.S.C. 867 and 870(a)) at  
Schedule 2; and .
(c) the schedules for the Department of Medicine and Surgery, Veterans Admin­
istration (38 U.S.C. 4107) at Schedule 3.

Sec. 2. Pay and Allowances for Members of the Uniformed Services.  Pursuant to  
the provisions of Section 1009 of Title 37 of the United States Code, the rates of  
monthly basic pay (37 U.S.C. 2 0 3 (a )), the rates of basic allowances for subsistence  
(37 U.S.C. 402), and the rates of basic allowances for quarters (37 U.S.C. 4 0 3 (a ))  
are adjusted,, as set forth at Schedule 4 attached hereto and made a. part hereof, for  
members of the uniformed services.

Sec. 3. Executive Salaries.  The Executive Salary Cost of Living Adjustment Act  
(Public Law 94— 82, 89 Stat. 419) provides for adjustments in the rates of pay and  
salaries, as set forth at the schedules attached hereto and made a part hereof, for the  
following:
(a) The Vice President (3 U.S.C. 104) and the Executive Schedule (5 U.S.C.  
5312— 5316) at Schedule 5;
(b) Congressional Salaries (2 U.S.C. 31) at Schedule 6; and
(c) Judicial Salaries (28 U.S.C. 5, 4 4 (d ), 135, 173, 213, 252, 792(b) and 11  
U.S.G. 6 8 (a )), at Schedule 7.

Sec. 4. Effective Date.  The adjustments in rates of monthly basic pay and basic  
allowances for subsistence and quarters for members of the uniformed services shall  
be effective on October 1,1976. AH other adjustments of salary or pay shall be effective  
on the first day of the first applicable pay period beginning on or after October 1, 1976.
Sec. 5. Superseded Orders.  Executive Order No. 11883 of October 6, 1975.

research_rationale: EO 11941 of October 1, 1976 (official text 41 FR 43889-43894, saved OCR text layer read in full: five sections and seven rate schedules ending with the filing line) adjusts statutory pay systems (s.1, Schedules 1-3), uniformed-services pay and allowances (s.2, Schedule 4) and executive, congressional and judicial salaries (s.3, Schedules 5-7), sets effective dates (s.4) and supersedes EO 11883 (s.5). Each schedule is inventoried as its own clause (heading quoted; the tables themselves are the operative rates). EO 11943 (October 25, 1976) corrected one figure in Schedule 3 (later event). EO 12010 of September 28, 1977 (42 FR 52365, read in full) section 4: 'Executive Order No. 11941 of October 1, 1976, is superseded', so every clause is terminated, but its rates take effect on pay-period dates that the held sources do not fix, and it does not cover Schedules 5-7. The current-law lead (28 U.S.C. 172 note) is a historical salary note ('formerly set out as a note under section 5332 of Title 5'), not a continuing basis, so it does not contradict the NO status. No first-end date is asserted. Partial claim.

research_rationale: EO 7921 (June 30, 1938) extended the existence of the Quetico-Superior Committee for four years, from June 30, 1938 to June 30, 1942. The Quetico-Superior Committee was created by EO 6783 (1934) for a limited period and kept alive by successive four-year extension orders (EOs 7921, 9213, 9741, 10134, 10541, 10767, 11031) and amended by EOs 9890, 10589 and 11031. EO 11342 of April 10, 1967 (32 FR 5827) established a committee of the same name anew (sec. 1), let it carry forward the old committee's uncompleted business (sec. 5) and in sec. 6 superseded EO 6783 and all nine continuing or amending orders; it states no effective date, so it took effect on signing. That supersession was a formal cleanup: each extension order had already run out on the fixed date it states, and the last extension (EO 11031 sec. 1) ended on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification disposition row for EO 6783 lists no continuation after EO 11031, the OFR catalog has no Quetico order between EO 11031 and EO 11342, and EO 11342 establishes the committee anew, so the committee lapsed on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification ('Superseded by EO 11342') and the OFR catalog note were used only as leads; the dates come from the order texts. Texts were checked against the text layer of the saved official Federal Register scans (fr-originals); no page-image comparison was made. This order's only operative provision is the extension itself, so its operation ended on 1942-06-30; the 1967 supersession is recorded as a later event.

research_rationale: EO 10541 (June 30, 1954) further extended the committee for four years from June 30, 1954 to June 30, 1958. The Quetico-Superior Committee was created by EO 6783 (1934) for a limited period and kept alive by successive four-year extension orders (EOs 7921, 9213, 9741, 10134, 10541, 10767, 11031) and amended by EOs 9890, 10589 and 11031. EO 11342 of April 10, 1967 (32 FR 5827) established a committee of the same name anew (sec. 1), let it carry forward the old committee's uncompleted business (sec. 5) and in sec. 6 superseded EO 6783 and all nine continuing or amending orders; it states no effective date, so it took effect on signing. That supersession was a formal cleanup: each extension order had already run out on the fixed date it states, and the last extension (EO 11031 sec. 1) ended on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification disposition row for EO 6783 lists no continuation after EO 11031, the OFR catalog has no Quetico order between EO 11031 and EO 11342, and EO 11342 establishes the committee anew, so the committee lapsed on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification ('Superseded by EO 11342') and the OFR catalog note were used only as leads; the dates come from the order texts. Texts were checked against the text layer of the saved official Federal Register scans (fr-originals); no page-image comparison was made. This order's only operative provision is the extension itself, so its operation ended on 1958-06-30; the 1967 supersession is recorded as a later event.

Murie (printed 'Glaus' in the text layer) to a vacancy, and amended EO 6783 accordingly. The Quetico-Superior Committee was created by EO 6783 (1934) for a limited period and kept alive by successive four-year extension orders (EOs 7921, 9213, 9741, 10134, 10541, 10767, 11031) and amended by EOs 9890, 10589 and 11031. The 1989 Codification disposition row for EO 6783 lists no continuation after EO 11031, the OFR catalog has no Quetico order between EO 11031 and EO 11342, and EO 11342 establishes the committee anew, so the committee lapsed on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification ('Superseded by EO 11342') and the OFR catalog note were used only as leads; the dates come from the order texts. Texts were checked against the text layer of the saved official Federal Register scans (fr-originals); no page-image comparison was made. The authority to consult and the amendment of EO 6783 had no term of their own and operated only while the committee existed, so they ceased with the committee on June 30, 1966. The appointment was a one-time act completed on issuance (if it were instead dated by the appointee's tenure, that tenure could not outlast the committee, so the whole-order end is unchanged). research_rationale: EO 10589 (January 15, 1955) appointed or continued Charles S. Kelly (chairman), Ernest C. Oberholtzer and Paul Clement as members, amended EO 6783 accordingly, and provided that the two designated members continue to be designated by and serve at the pleasure of the Secretaries of Agriculture and the Interior. The Quetico-Superior Committee was created by EO 6783 (1934) for a limited period and kept alive by successive four-year extension orders (EOs 7921, 9213, 9741, 10134, 10541, 10767, 11031) and amended by EOs 9890, 10589 and 11031. EO 11342 of April 10, 1967 (32 FR 5827) established a committee of the same name anew (sec. 1), let it carry forward the old committee's uncompleted business (sec. 5) and in sec. 6 superseded EO 6783 and all nine continuing or amending orders; it states no effective date, so it took effect on signing. That supersession was a formal cleanup: each extension order had already run out on the fixed date it states, and the last extension (EO 11031 sec. 1) ended on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification disposition row for EO 6783 lists no continuation after EO 11031, the OFR catalog has no Quetico order between EO 11031 and EO 11342, and EO 11342 establishes the committee anew, so the committee lapsed on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification ('Superseded by EO 11342') and the OFR catalog note were used only as leads; the dates come from the order texts. Texts were checked against the text layer of the saved official Federal Register scans (fr-originals); no page-image comparison was made. The amendment and the designated-member rule had no term of their own and ceased with the committee on June 30, 1966 (EO 11031 sec. 2(b) restated the same rule in 1962 without ending it). The appointment was a one-time act completed on issuance; EO 11031 sec. 2(a) re-appointed the same members for a fixed term ending June 30, 1966. Whole-order end: 1966-06-30.

research_rationale: EO 11031 (June 19, 1962) extended the committee for four years ending June 30, 1966 (sec. 1), re-appointed its three appointive members for a four-year period ending the same day (sec. 2(a)), continued the two designated members at the Secretaries' pleasure (sec. 2(b)) and amended EO 6783 accordingly (sec. 3). The Quetico-Superior Committee was created by EO 6783 (1934) for a limited period and kept alive by successive four-year extension orders (EOs 7921, 9213, 9741, 10134, 10541, 10767, 11031) and amended by EOs 9890, 10589 and 11031. EO 11342 of April 10, 1967 (32 FR 5827) established a committee of the same name anew (sec. 1), let it carry forward the old committee's uncompleted business (sec. 5) and in sec. 6 superseded EO 6783 and all nine continuing or amending orders; it states no effective date, so it took effect on signing. That supersession was a formal cleanup: each extension order had already run out on the fixed date it states, and the last extension (EO 11031 sec. 1) ended on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification disposition row for EO 6783 lists no continuation after EO 11031, the OFR catalog has no Quetico order between EO 11031 and EO 11342, and EO 11342 establishes the committee anew, so the committee lapsed on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification ('Superseded by EO 11342') and the OFR catalog note were used only as leads; the dates come from the order texts. Texts were checked against the text layer of the saved official Federal Register scans (fr-originals); no page-image comparison was made. Secs. 1 and 2(a) ended by their own terms on June 30, 1966; secs. 2(b) and 3 had no term of their own and ceased with the committee that day. The draft's EVENT_BEFORE_SIGNING conflicts came from a catalog note listing earlier extensions (EOs 10134, 10541, 10589, 10767) that predate and do not affect this order. Whole-order end: 1966-06-30.

research_rationale: EO 11768 (February 20, 1974) placed 16 positions in level IV (sec. 1) and 9 in level V (sec. 2), protected incumbents (sec. 3) and superseded EO 11708 (sec. 4). EO 11861 of May 21, 1975 (40 FR 22531) placed a new complete list of positions in levels IV and V of the Executive Schedule and in sec. 4 superseded 'Executive Order No. 11768 of February 20, 1974, as amended'; it states no effective date for itself (the only dates in it are the June 1, 1975 termination of one listed position), so it took effect on signing. The amending orders EOs 11774 (March 26, 1974), 11780 (April 22, 1974), 11831 (January 9, 1975) and 11843 (March 18, 1975, effective March 1, 1975) operated only as text inserted into EO 11768, so the supersession of EO 11768 'as amended' ended them too, except where an amendment had already been displaced. The 1989 Codification ('Superseded by EO 11861') and the OFR catalog notes were used as leads only; every date comes from the order texts, checked against the text layer of the saved official FR scans (no page-image comparison). Item-level ends: sec. 1(7) was replaced by EO 11774 on March 26, 1974; sec. 1(3), (12) and (15) were replaced and sec. 1(16) deleted by EO 11831 on January 9, 1975; every other placement, both lead-ins and sec. 3 ended with the supersession on May 21, 1975. Sec. 4 (supersession of EO 11708) was a one-time act complete on issuance. EO 11780's addition of sec. 2(10) is recorded as a later event on sec. 2. The draft's STATED_EFFECTIVE_DATE_DIFFERS conflicts are resolved: EO 11831 has no stated effective date (its 'March 1, 1975' is the termination date of the position it inserted) and EO 11843 is effective March 1, 1975. Whole-order end: 1975-05-21.

research_rationale: EO 8688 (February 19, 1941), under the act of October 17, 1940 (Public No. 872, 76th Congress), prescribed regulations for quarters allowances to Army enlisted men of the first three grades with dependents: definitions of dependent and children (para. 1) and the entitlement, effective as of October 17, 1940, measured by the non-travel quarters rates of EO 7293 'or any amendments thereto, issued under section 11' of the 1922 act, plus a lodging allowance for Philippine Scouts (para. 2). EO 9206 (7 FR 5851), signed July 27, 1942 under section 10 of the act of June 16, 1942 (Public Law 607, 77th Congress), prescribed new allowance regulations and in its closing paragraph superseded EO 8688, EO 8704 'as amended by Executive Order No. 8759' and EO 9105, and 'shall be effective as of June 1, 1942'. First_end uses that stated effective date, not the signing date. No earlier event ending any of these provisions was found: the OFR catalog notes record only the amendments by EOs 8759 and 9105 and the supersession by EO 9206. Catalog notes were used as leads only; the dates come from the order texts, checked against the text layer of the saved official FR scans (no page-image comparison). The rate cross-reference in para. 2a is read as reaching the rates of EO 8704, which replaced EO 7293's rates under the same section 11; on either reading the entitlement itself continued until the supersession. EO 9206's section on enlisted men of the first three grades with dependents re-enacted the substance under the 1942 act. Every clause ended on 1942-06-01; whole-order end 1942-06-01.

research_rationale: EO 8704 (March 4, 1941), under section 11 of the act of June 10, 1922, prescribed the allowances for quarters and subsistence for enlisted men of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Coast Guard, Coast and Geodetic Survey and Public Health Service not furnished quarters or rations in kind: Table I (station allowances) with two notes, Table II (travel allowances) with four notes, and a closing paragraph superseding EO 7293 and its amendments, effective on the date of the order except for continental quarters allowances (July 1, 1941). EO 8759 (May 24, 1941) added Exception No. 5 to Table I and EO 9105 (March 19, 1942) inserted a paragraph on advance payments; both are recorded as later events, not ends. EO 9206 (7 FR 5851), signed July 27, 1942 under section 10 of the act of June 16, 1942 (Public Law 607, 77th Congress), prescribed new allowance regulations and in its closing paragraph superseded EO 8688, EO 8704 'as amended by Executive Order No. 8759' and EO 9105, and 'shall be effective as of June 1, 1942'. First_end uses that stated effective date, not the signing date. No earlier event ending any of these provisions was found: the OFR catalog notes record only the amendments by EOs 8759 and 9105 and the supersession by EO 9206. Catalog notes were used as leads only; the dates come from the order texts, checked against the text layer of the saved official FR scans (no page-image comparison). The tables, notes and regulations ended on 1942-06-01. The closing supersession and deferred-effective-date provisions were one-time and complete on July 1, 1941. The text layer of this page interleaves columns; each clause quotes the verbatim fragments as printed (see text_note) and the clause inventory follows the printed structure. Whole-order end 1942-06-01.

EO 9206 (7 FR 5851), signed July 27, 1942 under section 10 of the act of June 16, 1942 (Public Law 607, 77th Congress), prescribed new allowance regulations and in its closing paragraph superseded EO 8688, EO 8704 'as amended by Executive Order No. 8759' and EO 9105, and 'shall be effective as of June 1, 1942'. The exception's own condition (the national emergency) had not ended by June 1, 1942, so its first end is the supersession of EO 8704 'as amended by Executive Order No. 8759'. EO 9206's Table I, item C, carries a similar emergency allowance under its own authority. Whole-order end 1942-06-01.

research_rationale: EO 11641 (January 28, 1972) had the Attorney General establish an Office for Drug Abuse Law Enforcement in the Department of Justice (sec. 1(a)), headed by a Director with the title Special Assistant Attorney General (sec. 1(b)) who also served as Special Consultant to the President (sec. 1(c)) and ran a concentrated federal enforcement program (sec. 1(d)); required consultation with the Special Action Office for Drug Abuse Prevention (sec. 2); placed the Director in level IV by amending EO 11248 sec. 1 (sec. 3); and required agency assistance (sec. 4). EO 11727 of July 6, 1973 (38 FR 18357) recites that Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1973, effective July 1, 1973, establishes the Drug Enforcement Administration into which both offices' functions would be merged; it revokes EO 11641 (sec. 2) and EO 11676 (sec. 3), directs the Attorney General to reassign their functions, abolish the offices and wind up their affairs (secs. 2, 3, 5), deletes both directors from level IV as listed in EO 11708 (sec. 4), and is 'effective as of July 1, 1973' (sec. 6). First_end uses that stated effective date, not the July 6 signing date. One earlier partial end (also noted by the OFR catalog, which records EO 11248 as revoked by EO 11708): sec. 3 of this order had inserted its director into EO 11248 sec. 1, and EO 11708 sec. 3 (March 23, 1973) revoked EO 11248 as amended except for level V positions, so sec. 3 ended on 1973-03-23 (EO 11708 sec. 1 placed the director anew, and EO 11727 sec. 4 later deleted that placement). The U.S. Code note under 21 U.S.C. 801 (release point 119-121), which reprints EO 11727, and the eCFR hits were read: they record the revocation and nothing continuing. The 1989 Codification disposition table and the OFR catalog note were used as leads only; the dates come from the order texts, checked against the text layer of the saved official FR scans (no page-image comparison). Whole-order end 1973-07-01.

(b ) The Director shall be responsible for the development and main­
tenance of a National Narcotics Intelligence System. In developing that 
system, the Director shall call upon other agencies of the Government 
to provide him with information, and such agencies shall, to the extent 
permitted by law, provide the Director with all information that is 
pertinent to the development and maintenance of a National Narcotics 
Intelligence System. The Director shall also call upon State and local 
agencies to provide him with such information.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 11727 directs the Attorney General to reassign the office's functions, abolish the office and wind up its affairs, in step with Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1973, which merged these functions into the Drug Enforcement Administration. Those functions continue under the reorganization plan and the Attorney General's authority, not under this order; no clause of this order survives.

source.quote:
Se c. 5. The Attorney General shall provide for the winding up of the 
affairs of the two offices and for the reassignment of their functions.
source.excerpt:
Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1973, which becomes effective on 
July 1, 1973, among other things establishes a Drug Enforcement 
Administration in the Department of Justice. In my message to the 
Congress transmitting that plan, I stated that all functions of the Office 
for Drug Abuse Law Enforcement (established pursuant to Executive 
Order No. 11641 of January 28, 1972) and the Office of National 
Narcotics Intelligence (established pursuant to Executive Order No. 
11676 of July 27, 1972) would, together with other related functions, 
be merged in the new Drug Enforcement Administration.

research_rationale: EO 11676 (July 27, 1972) had the Attorney General establish an Office of National Narcotics Intelligence in the Department of Justice headed by a Director (sec. 1(a)) responsible for a National Narcotics Intelligence System with information duties on other agencies (sec. 1(b)) and power to share intelligence under the Attorney General's supervision (sec. 1(c)); required cooperation with the Office for Drug Abuse Law Enforcement (sec. 2); placed the Director in level IV by amending EO 11248 sec. 1 (sec. 3); and required agency assistance (sec. 4). EO 11727 of July 6, 1973 (38 FR 18357) recites that Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1973, effective July 1, 1973, establishes the Drug Enforcement Administration into which both offices' functions would be merged; it revokes EO 11641 (sec. 2) and EO 11676 (sec. 3), directs the Attorney General to reassign their functions, abolish the offices and wind up their affairs (secs. 2, 3, 5), deletes both directors from level IV as listed in EO 11708 (sec. 4), and is 'effective as of July 1, 1973' (sec. 6). First_end uses that stated effective date, not the July 6 signing date. One earlier partial end (also noted by the OFR catalog, which records EO 11248 as revoked by EO 11708): sec. 3 of this order had inserted its director into EO 11248 sec. 1, and EO 11708 sec. 3 (March 23, 1973) revoked EO 11248 as amended except for level V positions, so sec. 3 ended on 1973-03-23 (EO 11708 sec. 1 placed the director anew, and EO 11727 sec. 4 later deleted that placement). The U.S. Code note under 21 U.S.C. 801 (release point 119-121), which reprints EO 11727, and the eCFR hits were read: they record the revocation and nothing continuing. The 1989 Codification disposition table and the OFR catalog note were used as leads only; the dates come from the order texts, checked against the text layer of the saved official FR scans (no page-image comparison). Whole-order end 1973-07-01.

research_rationale: EO 11948 (December 20, 1976, effective December 31, 1976) continued thirteen advisory committees until December 31, 1978 (sec. 1(a)-(m)), assigned the President's Federal Advisory Committee Act functions for them to the listed agency heads (sec. 2), revoked EO 11868 effective January 16, 1977 (sec. 3), revoked EOs 11667, 11809 and 11860 and superseded EO 11827 (sec. 4). Earlier partial ends found by reading the acting texts: EO 12007 (August 22, 1977) terminated the Citizens' Advisory Council on the Status of Women, the Citizens' Advisory Committee on Environmental Quality, the Advisory Council for Minority Enterprise and the Consumer Advisory Council and in sec. 6 superseded subsections (a), (g), (i) and (j) of sec. 1; EO 12029 (December 14, 1977) terminated the Quetico-Superior Committee and in sec. 2 superseded subsection (e). Neither states an effective date, so each took effect on signing. The remaining continuances ran 'until December 31, 1978', the same day EO 12110 (signed December 28, 1978) took effect under its sec. 1-105 and superseded this order (sec. 1-104); sec. 2 ended then too. Secs. 3, 4 and 5 were one-time acts complete on January 16, 1977 and December 31, 1976. research_rationale: EO 10559 (Sept. 8, 1954; 19 FR 5879) has two operative sections: sec. 1 delegates to the Budget Director the President's authority to allocate the 'Expenses of Management Improvement' appropriation (and any reenactment); sec. 2 requires reports and direction of the funded activities. Neither section has an expiry or condition; the delegation follows the paragraph as reenacted, and EO 11230 sec. 1(23) itself delegates the paragraph as reenacted in the Executive Office Appropriation Act 1965, so the authority was still live in 1965. No amendment of EO 10559 is recorded in the OFR catalog edges or the 1989 Codification disposition table ('Superseded by EO 11230'). EO 11230 sec. 2(2) expressly supersedes EO 10559; EO 11230 states no effective date and so took effect on issuance, June 28, 1965. Both clauses therefore first ended on 1965-06-28, which is also the whole-order end. Savings: EO 11230 sec. 4 keeps prior actions and regulations in effect under EO 11230 and sec. 3(b) redirects references; the function itself passes to EO 11230 sec. 1(23). No current-law citation of EO 10559 was found (U.S. Code release 119-121, eCFR as of 2026-10-14).

research_rationale: EO 10766 (May 1, 1958; 23 FR 2981-2982) delegates to the Budget Director the President's authority under section 407(b) of the Act of Aug. 30, 1957 to approve regulations on rental of substandard housing for members of the uniformed services (sec. 1, which also lets such regulations take effect between Dec. 31, 1957 and the date section 407(b) ceases to be in force), extends it to amending or terminating such regulations (sec. 2) and requires reports from the Secretaries (third section, OCR-numbered 'Sec/ 2.'). The order's only time term is tied to section 407(b) remaining in force; EO 11230 sec. 1(22) re-delegates the same section 407(b) authority in 1965, which shows the statute had not ceased by then, so no earlier ending applies. No amendment is recorded (OFR catalog edges; 1989 Codification 'Superseded by EO 11230'). EO 11230 sec. 2(4) supersedes EO 10766, effective on issuance June 28, 1965; all three clauses and the order first ended on 1965-06-28. Savings pass to EO 11230 under its secs. 3(b) and 4. No current-law citation was found.

research_rationale: EO 10836 (Sept. 8, 1959; 24 FR 7269) amends section 1 (Part I) of EO 10530 by substituting paragraph (l) (approvals under section 11 of the Act of June 6, 1924, as renumbered and amended in 1952) and adding paragraph (o) (Alaska Omnibus Act sec. 44(a) transitional grants and sec. 44(b) interim services and fund allocation). Neither clause carries an expiry. The statutory life of the Alaska Omnibus Act sec. 44 grant authority was not checked against the Statutes at Large (not held in the project); EO 11230 sec. 1(26) re-delegated the same sec. 44(a) and 44(b) authorities on June 28, 1965, which indicates they were still treated as live, so no earlier statutory lapse is asserted. The OFR catalog and the 1989 Codification ('Amended EO 10530 ... Superseded by EO 11230') show no other later event. EO 11230 sec. 2 supersedes Part I of EO 10530 (item 1) and EO 10836 (item 6), effective on issuance June 28, 1965. All clauses first ended on 1965-06-28, the whole-order end. The only current-law hit is the 3 U.S.C. 301 note's status line for EO 10530 ('as amended by ... Ex. Ord. No. ...'), an amendment history of the host order, not a current predicate for this order; the provisions it added to section 1 (Part I) of EO 10530 were superseded with Part I by EO 11230 sec. 2(1).

research_rationale: EO 10889 (Oct. 5, 1960; 25 FR 9633) adds paragraphs (p), (q) and (r) to section 1 (Part I) of EO 10530 and, in sec. 2, supersedes four 1960 presidential letters under Alaska Omnibus Act sec. 45(a). Clause by clause: (p)(1), the determination power under sec. 45(a), ran until EO 11164 substituted the whole of paragraph (p) on Aug. 1, 1964 (EO 11164 states no effective date; effective on issuance). (p)(2), the conveyance power, was delegated only 'until July 1, 1964' by this order's own words, so it first ended on 1964-07-01 by its own terms, before EO 11164 restored a conveyance power without that limit. (q) was replaced in full by EO 10960 on Aug. 21, 1961 (substitution 'to read as follows', effective on issuance). Sec. 2's supersession of the four letters was completed on issuance, Oct. 5, 1960 (spent; recorded as its first end). (r) and the enacting words continued until EO 11230 sec. 2 superseded Part I of EO 10530 (item 1) and EO 10889 (item 7), effective on issuance June 28, 1965. Convention: a clause whose whole text is replaced by a later order's substituted text ends on that order's effective date; the substituted text is the later order's clause. A first_end that is a limit in the order itself uses the first day the clause no longer applied. Whole-order end = latest clause end = 1965-06-28. The OFR catalog also records EO 10960 as amending this order; the 1989 Codification row reads 'Amended EO 10530. Amended by EO 10960 ... Superseded by EO 11230'. The only current-law hit is the 3 U.S.C. 301 note's status line for EO 10530 ('as amended by ... Ex. Ord. No. ...'), an amendment history of the host order, not a current predicate for this order; the provisions it added to section 1 (Part I) of EO 10530 were superseded with Part I by EO 11230 sec. 2(1). The clause inventory is quoted from the official FR scan (the draft's clauses came from a mirror transcription and were not used).

savings_residuals.reason: EO 11230 sec. 4 keeps in effect all actions taken and regulations prescribed or approved in the matters covered by its sec. 1 (which re-delegates the same presidential functions to the Director of the Bureau of the Budget) until amended or revoked under EO 11230; sec. 3(b) redirects references to superseded orders to the corresponding provision of EO 11230. The functions therefore pass to EO 11230 and past actions survive under it; nothing continues to rest on this order. Paragraph (2) (section 4(g) of EO 10530, Alaska Omnibus Act sec. 57 grants) was superseded earlier by EO 11196 sec. 2(4), whose sec. 1(6) re-delegates that authority to the Housing and Home Finance Administrator and whose sec. 4 keeps prior actions in effect; EO 11230 sec. 1(24)-(25) re-delegates the subsection (x) and (y) authorities.

research_rationale: EO 11184 (Oct. 13, 1964; 29 FR 14155) amends EO 10530 in two ways: paragraph (1) adds subsections (x) (quarters regulations under sec. 6 of the Act of Aug. 20, 1964) and (y) (California offshore-islands allowance under the Act of Aug. 31, 1964) to section 1 (Part I, Budget Director); paragraph (2) adds subsection (g) to section 4 (Alaska Omnibus Act sec. 57 grants, plan approval, reports and access to records). EO 11196 sec. 2(4) superseded 'so much of Executive Order No. 11184 ... as added paragraph (g) to Section 4', effective on issuance Feb. 2, 1965 (signature date garbled in the OCR; filing line and OFR catalog give Feb. 2, 1965), so clause para2-g first ended on 1965-02-02. The rest continued until EO 11230 sec. 2 superseded Part I of EO 10530 (item 1) and all of EO 11184 (item 14), effective on issuance June 28, 1965. Whole-order end = latest clause end = 1965-06-28. The 1989 Codification row reads 'Amended by EO 10530, 11196 ... Superseded by EO 11230' (the first entry is the OCR of 'Amended EO 10530'). The only current-law hit is the 3 U.S.C. 301 note's status line for EO 10530 ('as amended by ... Ex. Ord. No. ...'), an amendment history of the host order, not a current predicate for this order; the subsections it added were superseded by EO 11196 sec. 2(4) and EO 11230 sec. 2(1), (14).

research_rationale: EO 8546 (Sept. 24, 1940; 5 FR 3817-3818) creates the Defense Communications Board (para. 1), gives it planning functions for national emergencies (para. 2), sets its chairmanship and secretary (para. 3), its scope and broadcasting studies (para. 4), committees (paras. 5-6), consultation (para. 7), the advisory role of the Interdepartment Radio Advisory Committee during war or national emergency (para. 8) and reporting to the President (para. 9). Later events: EO 8960 (Dec. 6, 1941) substituted the Treasury officer named in paras. 1 and 3; EO 9183 (June 15, 1942) renamed the Board the Board of War Communications and amended this order accordingly; neither ended a clause (word substitutions; the clauses continue as amended). EO 8964 and EO 9089 gave the Board further powers without amending this order. The orders rest on wartime and emergency powers (Communications Act sec. 606 and the national emergency); neither the orders nor sec. 606 had lapsed before Feb. 24, 1947: the state of war declared in December 1941 had not been terminated, and no concurrent resolution ending the sec. 606 powers is recorded in the bounded sources; no earlier presidential order ending any of these provisions appears in the OFR catalog or the saved order texts. EO 9831 (Feb. 24, 1947; 12 FR 1363) para. 1 abolishes the Board, created 'as the Defense Communications Board by Executive Order No. 8546', and para. 2 revokes EO 8546; it states no effective date, so it took effect on issuance. Every clause therefore first ended on 1947-02-24, the whole-order end. The two current-law hits (47 U.S.C. 606 note) print EO 9831 itself, which confirms the abolition and revocation; no current predicate. The 1989 Codification row: 'Amended by EOs 8960, 9183 ... Revoked by EO 9831'.

research_rationale: EO 8964 (Dec. 10, 1941; 6 FR 6367-6368) directs the Defense Communications Board to exercise the President's Communications Act sec. 606 powers over radio stations (enacting words) under eleven regulations (allocation plans, designation and classes of stations for government use or closure, agency reporting, limits, continued private operation, just compensation, relinquishment, priority of communications, definitions, publication). None has its own expiry; para. 8 lets the Board relinquish control case by case, which ends particular uses, not the clauses. EO 9183 (June 15, 1942) renamed the Board and amended this order accordingly (no clause ended). The orders rest on wartime and emergency powers (Communications Act sec. 606 and the national emergency); neither the orders nor sec. 606 had lapsed before Feb. 24, 1947: the state of war declared in December 1941 had not been terminated, and no concurrent resolution ending the sec. 606 powers is recorded in the bounded sources; no earlier presidential order ending any of these provisions appears in the OFR catalog or the saved order texts. EO 9831 para. 2 revokes EO 8964, effective on issuance Feb. 24, 1947; every clause and the order first ended on 1947-02-24. Counterevidence: the current-law hit (47 U.S.C. 606 note) states that EO 8964 'was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 9831, eff. Feb. 24, 1947', confirming the date. 1989 Codification: 'Amended by EO 9183 ... Revoked by EO 9831'.

research_rationale: EO 9089 (Mar. 6, 1942; 7 FR 1777-1778) directs the Defense Communications Board to exercise the President's Communications Act sec. 606(d) powers over wire communication facilities (enacting words) under ten regulations parallel to EO 8964's radio regulations. Sec. 606(d), as quoted in the order, runs 'during the period ending not later than six months after the termination of such state or threat of war' or an earlier date set by concurrent resolution; the state of war had not been terminated by Feb. 24, 1947 and no such concurrent resolution is recorded in the bounded sources, so the statutory period had not run. EO 9183 (June 15, 1942) renamed the Board and amended this order accordingly. The orders rest on wartime and emergency powers (Communications Act sec. 606 and the national emergency); neither the orders nor sec. 606 had lapsed before Feb. 24, 1947: the state of war declared in December 1941 had not been terminated, and no concurrent resolution ending the sec. 606 powers is recorded in the bounded sources; no earlier presidential order ending any of these provisions appears in the OFR catalog or the saved order texts. EO 9831 para. 2 revokes EO 9089, effective on issuance Feb. 24, 1947; every clause and the order first ended on 1947-02-24. 1989 Codification: 'Amended by EO 9183 ... Revoked by EO 9831'. No current-law citation. The draft's clause text quoted the footnote-joined number of EO 8546 (read as a non-existent order); the quotation is now split around it.

research_rationale: EO 9386 (Oct. 15, 1943, effective Nov. 1, 1943; 8 FR 14103-14105) prescribes under sec. 10 of the Pay Readjustment Act of 1942 the daily allowances for quarters and subsistence of enlisted men not furnished them in kind (Section I with paragraphs A, B, four exceptions, C and two notes), travel allowances (Section II), advance payment (Section III) and quarters allowances for enlisted men of the first three grades with dependents (Section IV), and supersedes EO 9206 as amended. It has no expiry of its own. Later events: EO 9561 (effective June 1, 1945, term later extended by EO 9744C to June 30, 1947) temporarily raised one subsistence rate in paragraph A and Exception No. 1 (clauses continue as amended); EO 9825 substituted the whole of Section II effective Feb. 15, 1947, so the original Section II first ended on 1947-02-15 (convention: wholesale substitution ends the original clause; the new text is EO 9825's own clause). The supersession of EO 9206 was completed on Nov. 1, 1943 (spent). All other clauses ran until EO 9871, which 'shall supersede Executive Order No. 9386 ... as amended by Executive Order No. 9561 ... and shall be effective from July 1, 1947'. EO 9871 was signed July 8, 1947; following its stated effective date the clauses first ended on 1947-07-01, the whole-order end. The OFR catalog edges and the 1989 Codification ('Amended by EOs 9561, 9825 ... Superseded by EO 9871') show no other event. The 1946 amendments of the Pay Readjustment Act (60 Stat. 853, 858, cited by EO 9871) were not checked against the Statutes at Large (not held); EO 9825 still amended this order in January 1947 and EO 9871 superseded it 'as amended', which indicates it remained the operative regulation until then. No current-law citation. The draft had no clause inventory; it is built here from the official FR scan.

operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Section II of Executive Order No. 9386, 
dated October 15, 1943, prescribing al­
lowances for quarters and subsistence to 
enlisted men not furnished quarters or 
rations in kind, is hereby amended, eflec-, 
tive as of February 15, 1947, to read as 
follows:
S ection  II
Men traveling on duty including de­
tentions not exceeding thirty-one days 
at any one place, when not furnished 
sleeping car, stateroom accommodations, 
o r other quarters, and rations in kind, 
shall be granted a daily allowance of 
$5.00: Provided, that when quarters in 
kind are furnished, they shall be entitled 
only to an allowance for subsistence at 
the rate of $1.00 per meal, and when 
subsistence is furnished they shall be 
entitled only to an allowance for quar­
ters at the rate of $2.00 per day; except 
that, where travel is performed by rail 
or water, the allowance for subsistence 
shall be $1.25 for each meal required to 
be taken in a dining car on a train or in 
a dining room on a steamer, and If 
quarters are not provided for the day 
of such travel, the allowance for. quar­
ters shall be $1.75 when an allowance for 
subsistence is so furnished for one meal, 
$1.50 when an allowance for subsistence 
is so furnished for two meals, or $1.25 
when an allowance for subsistence is so 
furnished for three meals. For the pur­
poses of this section, quarters in kind will 
be considered as furnished for the day 
of arrival at a permanent station.
Men absent under orders from their 
station upon duty which involves travel 
and also temporary detentions during 
the journey shail be deemed to be trav­
eling under orders during the entire pe­
riod of such absence including the day 
of departure therefrom and return there­
to. For periods of detention in excess of 
thirty-one days at any one place, the 
allowances preseribed in Section I shall 
govern after the thirty-first day.

operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Se c. 2. Functions and Responsibilities o f the Council,  (a ) The  
Council shall : ^
(1 ) Survey and assess the needs and prospects of the various arts  
throughout the United States, the means used to encourage creative  
activity and to afford opportunity for participation in and apprecia­
tion and enjoyment of the artSj and the relative roles of governmental  
and non-governmental institutions in relation to the arts ;
(2 ) Identify existing Federal legislation, policies and programs  
which directly or indirectly affect the arts, and evaluate their current  
and potential effects on the development of cultural opportunities and  
institutions and, except to the extent that responsibility may be vested  
by statute in other Federal advisory bodies, the character and quality  
of Federal activities in the field of the arts.;
(3) Submit reports and recommendations to the President on its  
own initiative or at the request of the President or the President’s  
Special Consultant on the Arts ;
(4) Encourage and facilitate the most effective use of resources  
available for support and development of the arts by advising and  
consulting with Federal, State and local agencies, civic and com­
munity organizations, educational institutions, foundations, and other  
interested organizations and institutions ; and
(5) Promote and stimulate public understanding and recognition  
of the importance of the arts and cultural institutions to our national  
welfare and our international interests.
