research_rationale: EO 11112 (June 12, 1963; 28 FR 6037-6038) establishes the President's Advisory Council on the Arts: establishment (1(a)), composition and terms (1(b)), chairman (1(c)), compensation (1(d)), meetings (1(e)), functions (2(a)(1)-(5)), hearing interested parties (2(b)), definition of the arts (2(c)), and agency liaison, information, assistance and GSA services (3(a)-(d)). No expiry or condition. EO 11124 (Oct. 28, 1963) substituted a new subsection (b) of Section 1 (two more ex officio members, up to forty private members), so the original 1(b) first ended on 1963-10-28 (convention: wholesale substitution ends the original clause; the new text is EO 11124's own clause). The National Council on the Arts Act of Sept. 3, 1964 did not itself abolish the Council; EO 11208 recites that it 'obviat[ed] the need' and then revokes EO 11112 and EO 11124, effective on issuance Mar. 24, 1965 (signature date garbled in the OCR; filing line Mar. 25, 1965 and OFR catalog Mar. 24, 1965). All other clauses first ended on 1965-03-24, the whole-order end. Whether private members were appointed before the Council's work was overtaken by the 1964 statute was not established from the bounded sources; the clauses' legal operation (the Council existed from the order, with ex officio federal members by office, and EO 11124 sec. 2 refers to sitting members) ran to the revocation, and no earlier presidential or statutory act ending the Council was found in the OFR catalog or the saved texts. 1989 Codification row: 'Amended by EO 11124 ... Revoked by EO 11208'. No current-law citation.

research_rationale: EO 11812 (Oct. 7, 1974, 'shall take effect October 1, 1974'; 39 FR 36307-36312) adjusts for members of the uniformed services the monthly basic pay (Sec. 1 tables), basic allowance for subsistence (Sec. 2) and basic allowance for quarters (Sec. 3), caps basic pay at Executive Schedule level V under 5 U.S.C. 5308 (Sec. 4), supersedes seven earlier uniformed-pay orders (Sec. 5) and sets its effective date (Sec. 6). It has no term of its own; its rates govern until the next adjustment. EO 11883 (signed Oct. 6, 1975) sec. 5 supersedes 'Executive Order No. 11812 of October 7, 1974', and its sec. 2 replacement rates for basic pay, subsistence and quarters 'shall be effective on October 1, 1975' (sec. 4). Every clause except Sec. 5 therefore first ended on 1975-10-01, the stated effective date in the acting instrument (the displacement was retroactive from that date to Oct. 6). Sec. 5's supersession of earlier orders was completed when the order issued on 1974-10-07 (spent). Whole-order end = 1975-10-01. All of this order concerns the uniformed services, so the agency-specific civilian pay-period dates in EO 11883 sec. 4 do not affect it. Counterevidence: the U.S. Code note under 37 U.S.C. 1009 states that EO 11812 'which provided for the adjustment of pay rates effective Oct. 1, 1974, was superseded by Ex. Ord. No. 11883' (history, not a predicate); the 1989 Codification row reads 'Superseded by EO 11883'. research_rationale: EO 11667 (April 19, 1972; 37 FR 7763) was read in the held official Federal Register scan (fr-originals OCR of PDF pages 7-8: heading, preamble, sections 1-3, signature block and FR Doc. 72-6171 filing line, so the text is complete). Its operative content is the establishment and composition of the President's Advisory Committee on the Environmental Merit Awards Program (sec. 1(a)), three committee functions (sec. 1(b)), the no-compensation/travel-expense rule (sec. 2) and EPA administrative support (sec. 3); the preamble is narrative. The order has no expiry, sunset, report deadline or condition. Because the committee existed before the Federal Advisory Committee Act took effect (January 5, 1973), it would have terminated on January 5, 1975 unless renewed; EO 11827 section 1(8) (held, 40 FR 1218) renewed it until January 5, 1977. Before that date EO 11948 (held, 41 FR 55706) section 4(a)(1) revoked EO 11667, and section 5 makes EO 11948 effective December 31, 1976; section 3's separate January 16, 1977 date applies only to EO 11868. So the first and only end of every clause is the revocation effective December 31, 1976, and the whole-order end is that date. The OFR catalog (revoked by EO 11948; continued by EO 11827) and the 1989 OFR Codification disposition table (continued by EO 11827; revoked by EO 11948) agree, and no other amendment, revocation or statute affecting the order was found in the bounded searches listed (no U.S. Code or eCFR citation of the order). Quotations are the scan's OCR text, kept as printed (soft hyphens at line ends).

research_rationale: EO 11864 (June 13, 1975; 40 FR 25579) was read in the held official FR scan (fr-originals OCR of PDF page 11, complete from heading to FR Doc. 75-15839 and footnote). It is a single amending sentence: effective June 1, 1975, section 1 of EO 11861 (placing positions in level IV of the Executive Schedule) is revised at paragraph (13) to read 'Adviser to the Secretary (Counselor, Economic Policy Board), Department of the Treasury, to terminate effective August 1, 1975' (the OCR renders the closing '1975.”' with its footnote mark as '1,197571'; EO 11877 section 1(b), held, quotes the same paragraph with the date as 'August 1, 1975'). The order therefore fixed its own end: the placement lapsed on August 1, 1975, and that is the first end of the only clause and the whole-order end. The formal supersession came a month later: EO 11877 (September 2, 1975; 40 FR 40797, held), which states no effective date, superseded EO 11864 (section 2) and replaced paragraph (13) with an open-ended placement (section 1(b)); it is recorded as a later event, not as the first end, following the rule that a formal supersession can follow an earlier cessation under the order's own terms. A current-law note at 5 U.S.C. 5317 and the OFR catalog describe the same history (the note says the paragraph was 'to terminate effective August 1, 1975' and was superseded by EO 11877); the 1989 OFR Codification table lists EO 11864 as amending EO 11861 and superseded by EO 11877. The machine current-law hits for this order are that historical note, not a continuing basis.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12148 revokes EO 10529 outright. Its only transition rule, section 2-302, lets the FEMA Director continue to perform functions transferred to him by section 1 of EO 12148 notwithstanding the revocations; that is a continuation of FEMA's own transferred functions, not a saving of EO 10529's terms, and EO 12148 does not re-enact the 40-hour limit or the other conditions of EO 10529. EO 10529 authorized time-limited training assignments while employees stayed in Federal pay status; it created no vested rights, and pay or travel already allowed for past assignments were completed. No surviving effect traceable to EO 10529 was found.

source.quote:
2- 302. Notwithstanding the revocations, revisions, codifications, and amend­
ments made by this Order, the Director may continue to perform the functions 
transferred to him by Section 1 of this Order, except where they may 
otherwise be inconsistent with the provisions of this Order.

research_rationale: EO 10529 (April 22, 1954; 19 FR 2397) was read in the held official FR scan (fr-originals OCR of PDF pages 1-3: heading, enacting clause, sections 1-5, Eisenhower signature and FR Doc. 54-3141). Section 2 begins on page 2397 and continues on page 2399 after the issue's contents pages; the clause is quoted from page 2399. Operative clauses: the Administrator's recommendation of volunteer Federal personnel for State and local pre-emergency civil-defense training (sec. 1); the agency head's year-to-year authorization (sec. 2) and its three conditions (sec. 2(a)-(c)); continued pay, status and travel (sec. 3); a construction rule (sec. 4); and two definitions (sec. 5). There is no expiry, condition or report duty. Later events, read in the held texts: EO 10773 (July 1, 1958), EO 10782 (effective August 26, 1958, renaming the office in EO 10773's substituted references) and EO 11051 section 603(d) (September 27, 1962) only substituted the responsible officials (ODCM/OCDM Director, then OEP Director or Secretary of Defense); they are amendments, not ends. Section 1's reference to section 3 of EO 10346 describes the arrangements the recommendations serve; EO 10346 was revoked by EO 11490 in 1969, but section 1 does not make its own authority depend on EO 10346, and EO 10529 was still being maintained by amendment, so that revocation is not treated as an end. EO 12148 (signed July 20, 1979; 44 FR 43239, held) section 5-104 revokes EO 10529, as amended, and section 6 makes the order effective July 15, 1979; that stated effective date is the first end of every clause and the whole-order end. The OFR catalog and the 1989 OFR Codification disposition table (amended by EOs 10773, 11051; revoked by EO 12148) agree. The current-law machine hits for this order are U.S. Code editorial notes recording its amendments and its revocation by EO 12148, not a continuing basis. No other amendment, revocation or statute affecting EO 10529 was found in the bounded searches listed.

research_rationale: EO 12489 (September 28, 1984; 49 FR 38927) was read in the held official FR scan (fr-originals OCR of PDF pages 9-10, complete from heading to FR Doc. 84-26328). The draft's clause list came from a mirror transcription; the inventory here was rebuilt from the official scan: the section 1 continuance term ('continued until September 30, 1985, unless terminated at a prior date by appropriate Executive order'), the eleven committee continuances (a)-(k), the section 2 continuance of the International Private Enterprise Task Force until December 31, 1984, and the section 3 delegation of the President's FACA functions to agency heads. Ends: section 2 expired by its own terms on December 31, 1984; no later continuance of the Task Force exists in the saved catalog (EO 12395 is noted only as continued by EOs 12399 and 12489 and revoked by EO 12534), and EO 12534 section 3(c) revoked EO 12395 as an order whose committee had terminated. None of the eleven section 1 committees was terminated before September 30, 1985: EO 12534 section 1 (held) continues all eleven again, and the catalog shows no intervening revocation. EO 12534 (September 30, 1985; 50 FR 40319, held) section 4 supersedes EO 12489 and section 5 makes it effective September 30, 1985, which is also the last day of EO 12489's own continuance term; that date is the first end of section 1, its items and section 3, and the whole-order end. The OFR catalog (superseded by EO 12534) and the 1989 OFR Codification disposition table (superseded by EO 12534) agree; no U.S. Code or eCFR citation of EO 12489 was found.

unresolved_material_gaps: first_end of every clause left open: the Committee was established on September 30, 1974, after the Federal Advisory Committee Act took effect, so under FACA section 14 it terminated two years after establishment (about September 30, 1976) unless renewed before then. EO 11827 section 2 (held), which continued the post-1973 presidential committees expiring before January 5, 1977, does not list it, and no renewal has been found; section 5 of the order gave the Treasury the Committee's FACA functions, so a Treasury charter renewal is possible and has not been searched. If not renewed, the Committee ended on or about September 30, 1976 and the EO 11948 revocation effective December 31, 1976 was a cleanup. Needed: Treasury FACA charter renewal or termination notice for the President's Labor-Management Committee (Federal Register, September-December 1976), and the exact FACA two-year computation.

The machine conflict NO_ORDER_CITED_IN_CURRENT_LAW is resolved: 16 CFR part 1027, 45 CFR part 1179 and 5 CFR part 1215 cite 'E.O. 11809 (redesignated E.O. 12107)' as authority for salary-offset rules under 5 U.S.C. 5514, which is evidently a misprint for EO 11609 (the 5 U.S.C. 5514 delegation order redesignated by EO 12107); it is not a continuing basis for this Labor-Management Committee order.

research_rationale: EO 11809 (September 30, 1974; 39 FR 35565) was read in the held official FR scan (fr-originals OCR of PDF page 15, heading to FR Doc. 74-23127). Its five operative sections establish the President's Labor-Management Committee (eight labor, eight management members and a neutral coordinator), state its study-and-advice functions, direct it to encourage sector labor-management committees, direct agency cooperation and assign FACA functions to the Treasury. EO 11948 (held) section 4(a)(2) revokes it, effective December 31, 1976 under section 5. Because the Committee was created after January 5, 1973 and is absent from EO 11827's list of continued post-1973 committees, it may have terminated under the FACA two-year rule about three months before the formal revocation; the first ends are therefore left open rather than taken from the revocation. The OFR catalog (revoked by EO 11948; see EO 11849) and the 1989 OFR Codification table (revoked by EO 11948) agree on the formal history.

Chapter 53 of Title 5 of the United States Code, the rates of basic pay and

the provisions of Section 1009 of Title 37 of the United States Code, the rates  
of monthly basic pay (37 U.S.C. 203(a) and (c)), the rates of basic allowances  
for subsistence (37 U.S.C. 402), and the rates of basic allowances for quarters  
(37 U.S.C. 403(a)) are adjusted, as set forth at Schedule 4 attached hereto and  
made a part hereof, for members of the uniformed services.

Act (Public Law 94-82, 89 j>tat. 419) provides for adjustments in the rates of  
pay and salaries as set forth at the schedules attached hereto and made a part  
hereof, for the following:

(a) The Vice President (3 U.S.C. 104) and the Executive Schedule (5  
U.S.C. 5312-5316) at Schedule 5;
(b) Congressional Salaries (2 U.S.C. 31) at Schedule 6; and

(c) Judicial Salaries (28 U.S.C. 5, 44(d), 135, 173, 213, 252, 792(b) and 11  
U.S.C. 68(a)), at Schedule 7.

allowances for subsistence and quarters for members of the uniformed ser­
vices shall be effective on October 1, 1978. All other adjustments of salary or  
pay shall be effective on the first day of the first applicable pay period  
beginning on or after October 1, 1978. %

1977 is superseded.

research_rationale: EO 11992 (May 24, 1977; 42 FR 27195-27196, held official FR scan text) established the Committee on Selection of Federal Judicial Officers, an advisory committee under the Federal Advisory Committee Act. All fourteen operative clauses (Secs. 1-8, subsections separated) are quoted verbatim from the held OCR text. The order set its own end in Sec. 8 (termination on December 31, 1978 unless sooner extended); that end did not occur because EO 12110 (sec. 1-101(i), effective December 31, 1978) continued the Committee until December 31, 1980, and EO 12258 (sec. 1-101(g), effective December 31, 1980) continued it until December 31, 1982, so the chain is unbroken. Before that extended term ran out, EO 12305 of May 5, 1981 (46 FR 25421, item (b)) revoked EO 11992 and terminated the Committee; EO 12305 states no other effective date, so every clause's first end is May 5, 1981, which is also the whole-order end. No amendment of EO 11992 was found (OFR 1989 disposition table: 'Continued by EOs 12110, 12258; Revoked by EO 12305'; USC note at 28 U.S.C. pt. I agrees). The revocation leaves no savings or residual effect.

research_rationale: EO 12059 (May 11, 1978; 43 FR 20949-20951, held official FR scan text) re-established the United States Circuit Judge Nominating Commission (thirteen panels). Eighteen operative clauses are quoted verbatim; Sec. 6(b) is quoted in two segments because the page break inserts FR page furniture. Sec. 3(b) was rewritten by EO 12097 sec. 1-301 (November 8, 1978), a partial amendment recorded as a later event. The order's own end (Sec. 8: December 31, 1978 unless extended) was overtaken by EO 12110 sec. 1-101(j) (effective December 31, 1978; continued to December 31, 1980) and EO 12258 sec. 1-101(i) (effective December 31, 1980; continued to December 31, 1982). EO 12305 of May 5, 1981, item (a), revoked 'Executive Order No. 12059 ... as amended' and terminated the Commission, with no other effective date, so every continuing clause ends on May 5, 1981, the whole-order end. Sec. 9 (revocation of EO 11972 and EO 11993) operated once on issuance and is recorded as spent on May 11, 1978; its formal end with the order on May 5, 1981 is a later event, and that revocation did not revive the earlier orders. The clause-drafts identity quarantine (the body cites its own number) is resolved: the held page shows the heading 'Executive Order 12059 - May 11,1978' on 43 FR 20949. USC note at 28 U.S.C. 44 and the OFR 1989 table agree (revoked by EO 12305). No savings provision exists.

research_rationale: EO 12064 (June 5, 1978; 43 FR 24661-24662, held official FR scan text) established the United States Tax Court Nominating Commission as a FACA advisory committee. All fifteen numbered operative provisions (1-101 to 1-403) are quoted verbatim. No amendment was found. The order's own end (1-403: December 31, 1978 unless sooner extended) was overtaken by EO 12110 sec. 1-101(l) (effective December 31, 1978, continued to December 31, 1980) and EO 12258 sec. 1-101(j) (effective December 31, 1980, continued to December 31, 1982). EO 12305 of May 5, 1981, item (d), revoked the order and terminated the Commission, effective on signing; every clause therefore first ends on May 5, 1981, the whole-order end. research_rationale: EO 11708 (March 23, 1973; 38 FR 7979-7980, held official FR scan text) placed fourteen positions in level IV (Sec. 1), continued eight in level V (Sec. 2) and revoked EO 11248 except for the Sec. 2 positions (Sec. 3). Sec. 1 and Sec. 2 were amended item by item by EO 11715 (April 24, 1973), EO 11727 Sec. 4 (deleting items (6) and (7), effective as of July 1, 1973 under its Sec. 6) and EO 11736 (August 6, 1973); these are partial amendments recorded as later events, not ends of the clauses, which continued as amended. EO 11768 of February 20, 1974, Sec. 4, superseded 'Executive Order No. 11708 of March 23, 1973, as amended'; it states no effective date, so Sec. 1 and Sec. 2 first end on February 20, 1974, the whole-order end. Sec. 3 operated once on issuance and is recorded as spent on March 23, 1973. The draft's QUARANTINED_RELATIONSHIP_CONFLICT (Stage 19 causal queue) is resolved: its four live leads are exactly the EO 11715, 11727 and 11736 amendments and the EO 11768 supersession read here, and its ten quarantined leads (EOs 11389, 11393, 11409, 11441, 11581, 11587, 11604, 11634, 11676, 11699, flagged PREDECESSOR_NOT_EARLIER_THAN_ACTOR) are orders issued before EO 11708 (most of them amendments of EO 11248), which cannot act on a later order; none ends EO 11708 earlier. The 21 U.S.C. 801 note hit is the printed text of EO 11727. OFR 1989 table: 'Amended by EOs 11715, 11727, 11736. Superseded by EO 11768'.

research_rationale: EO 11872 (July 21, 1975; 40 FR 30619, held official FR scan text) has one operative clause: it amends Sec. 1 of EO 11861 by adding item '(14) Executive Vice President, Export-Import Bank' to level IV of the Executive Schedule. EO 11983 of May 4, 1977 (42 FR 23127) deleted that item from EO 11861 (Sec. 1(b)) and revoked EO 11872 (Sec. 2); it states no effective date, so the clause first ends on May 4, 1977, the whole-order end. The deletion in EO 11983 Sec. 1(b) names item (14) in its original wording, so the item was still in place until then. OFR 1989 table: 'Amended EO 11861. Revoked by EO 11983'; the USC note at 5 U.S.C. 5317 lists it only among the amendments of EO 11861. No savings provision.

research_rationale: EO 9206 (July 27, 1942; 7 FR 5851-5853, held official FR scan text) prescribed the regulations for enlisted men's quarters and subsistence allowances under section 10 of the Act of June 16, 1942. The text runs over three pages interrupted by the FR contents listing; nine operative clauses are quoted verbatim (Table I with its rate block, which the OCR separates from the labels, its two notes, Table II, its four notes, the advance-payment rule, the department heads' rule-making authority, the dependants' quarters allowance, the dependant definition, and the supersession of EO 8688 and EO 8704 as amended, effective as of June 1, 1942). EO 9295 (effective as of January 1, 1943) amended paragraph C of Table I, a partial amendment recorded as a later event. EO 9386 of October 15, 1943 superseded 'Executive Order No. 9206 of July 27, 1942, as amended by Executive Order No. 9295' and is 'effective as of November 1, 1943'; that is the first end of every continuing clause and the whole-order end. The order has no expiry or condition of its own that ended it earlier, and no later order in the corpus amends or ends it before November 1943. The supersession clause operated once on issuance (recorded as spent on July 27, 1942, the signing date, since a first end cannot precede signing although its effect ran from June 1, 1942). The OFR 1989 table agrees ('Amended by EO 9295. Superseded by EO 9386').

research_rationale: EO 10880 (June 7, 1960; 25 FR 5131, held official FR scan text) allowed indefinite and temporary employees meeting stated service conditions to have their appointments converted to career or career-conditional appointments. Six operative clauses are quoted verbatim (Sec. 1(a) with its conditions (i)-(v), Sec. 1(b) postal substitutes, Sec. 2 definitions, Sec. 3 returning service members, Sec. 4 exclusions, Sec. 5 rule-making). The order's own terms close the agency-recommendation window for Sec. 1(a) one year after its date, but set no date by which conversions had to be completed (Sec. 1(b) conversions wait for career substitute vacancies), and Sec. 3 stays open for any qualifying service member re-employed after discharge; no earlier cessation can therefore be proved from the order itself, and the recommendation deadline is not treated as an end. EO 12107 (effective January 1, 1979) redesignated the Civil Service Commission as the Office of Personnel Management in this order, confirming it was still treated as in force. EO 12608 of September 9, 1987, Sec. 1, revoked it (no separate effective date), which is the first end of every clause and the whole-order end; the same section preserves 'benefits already conferred'. USC note at 5 U.S.C. 3301 and the OFR 1989 table agree.

research_rationale: EO 12295 (February 24, 1981; 46 FR 14113, held official FR scan text) has one operative sentence: under section 126a(2) of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 the President, having made the statutory determination and notified Congress, extends the period for continued peaceful nuclear cooperation with EURATOM (already extended by EO 12193) 'to March 10, 1982'. That fixed end date is the order's own term, not a reporting deadline: when it arrived the extension the order granted was used up. EO 12351 of March 9, 1982 gave a new, separate extension to March 10, 1983 (recorded as a later event; it does not amend EO 12295), and the series continued by annual orders. The 1987 revocation by EO 12608 Sec. 1 therefore follows an earlier actual cessation and is recorded as a later formal event. First end of the clause and whole-order end: March 10, 1982, by expiry under the order's own terms. The USC note at 42 U.S.C. 2155 ('extended the period ... to Mar. 10, 1982') and the OFR 1989 table ('Revoked by EO 12608') are consistent with this.

research_rationale: EO 11414 (June 11, 1968; 33 FR 8645-8647, held official FR scan text) adjusted the monthly basic pay of the uniformed services under section 8 of Public Law 90-207, 'effective on July 1, 1968'. Its operative content is one adjusting sentence with four rate tables and three footnote rules (service-chief special rate, the O-1 to O-3 scope rule, senior enlisted adviser special rate); the sentence and footnotes are quoted verbatim, the table figures are cited by page because the OCR scatters them. The order had no expiry, but its rates were the ones next adjusted: EO 11475 adjusted the same rates for every grade, with new footnote rates, 'effective on July 1, 1969'. From that date the 1968 rates no longer governed pay, so every clause first ends on July 1, 1969 (implied supersession by the later adjustment), the whole-order end. EO 11812 Sec. 5(1) later superseded EO 11414 expressly, effective October 1, 1974 (Sec. 6); that cleanup supersession is recorded as a later event, not as the first end. The OFR 1989 table ('Superseded by EO 11812') and the 37 U.S.C. 203 note list it among the pre-1974 pay orders.

research_rationale: EO 11475 (June 16, 1969; 34 FR 9609-9611, held official FR scan text) adjusted the uniformed services' monthly basic pay under section 8 of Public Law 90-207 'effective on July 1, 1969': one adjusting sentence, four rate tables and three footnote rules, quoted verbatim (table figures cited by page; OCR scatters them). EO 11525 of April 15, 1970 adjusted the same rates for every grade with new footnote rates and Sec. 3 'This order shall take effect January 1, 1970'; from that date (retroactively, as the acting instrument states) the 1969 rates no longer governed pay, so every clause first ends on January 1, 1970, the whole-order end. The express supersession by EO 11812 Sec. 5(2), effective October 1, 1974, is a later cleanup event. No amendment of EO 11475 was found. OFR 1989 table: 'Superseded by EO 11812'.

research_rationale: EO 11638 (December 22, 1971; 36 FR 24913-24915, held official FR scan text) adjusted the uniformed services' monthly basic pay, Sec. 2 'This order shall take effect January 1, 1972': one adjusting section, four rate tables and three footnote rules, quoted verbatim (table figures cited by page). EO 11692 adjusted the same rates for every grade. As issued (December 15, 1972) EO 11692 took effect January 1, 1973; EO 11778 of April 12, 1974 rewrote its Sec. 2 to 'This order shall take effect October 1, 1972', so under the acting instrument as it now stands the 1971 rates were displaced from October 1, 1972. That date is recorded as the first end of every clause and the whole-order end; the original January 1, 1973 displacement is recorded as a later event so the reviewer sees both readings (if the reviewer prefers the date first in force, every clause and the whole-order end move to January 1, 1973). EO 11812 Sec. 5(5), effective October 1, 1974, later superseded EO 11638 expressly (cleanup, later event). OFR 1989 table: 'Superseded by EO 11812'.

research_rationale: PARTIAL. EO 8744 (April 24, 1941; 6 FR 2118-2119, held official FR scan text, closing tag '[No. 8744]') has a single operative paragraph: an incumbent of a position covered into the classified service by section 1 of EO 8743 who is involuntarily separated by reduction in force, abolition of the position or liquidation of the agency between the date of EO 8743 and the effective date of its section 1 may acquire a classified status for transfer, provided (among other things) that 'he obtains such transfer within one year from the date of his separation'. By its own terms the authorization could therefore operate only for separations up to the effective date of section 1 of EO 8743 (January 1, 1942 under EO 8743 Sec. 2, earlier for positions that fell vacant after June 30, 1941) and transfers within one year after them. The EO 12608 revocation of September 9, 1987 is a formal cleanup that follows this earlier cessation and is recorded as a later event, not the first end. The exact last day cannot yet be fixed: EO 8743 Sec. 2 was itself amended (EOs 9230, 9358, 9678, 9712 and others touch EO 8743) and it is not established whether any amendment moved the effective date of its section 1; and a transfer deadline is a condition of eligibility, so the date must be fixed from the text, not inferred.

research_rationale: EO 9172 (May 22, 1942) created a National Railway Labor Panel 'for the duration of the war and six months thereafter' and let its chairman form three-member emergency boards (paras. 1-3; 7 FR 3913-3914, read in the held govinfo scan). Before taking the revocation as the first end I checked the order's own term: the state of war with Germany and Japan had not been terminated in August 1947 (the President's proclamation of December 31, 1946 ended only hostilities), so the Panel's own term had not run, and EO 9883's recital confirms the Panel still existed. EO 9883 (12 FR 5481) revokes the order outright, states no effective date and has no savings clause, so every paragraph ended on its signing date, August 11, 1947. The U.S. Code and eCFR machine searches found no current citation.

That completed revocation therefore continues, but its continuing basis is EO 10123's non-revival sentence, an independent later source, not EO 9635. research_rationale: EO 9635 (September 29, 1945) reorganized the Navy Department in ten numbered paragraphs, read in the held govinfo scan of 10 FR 12419 and its continuation on 12421. It has no expiry or condition of its own. Its main statutory basis, Title I of the First War Powers Act, was by its sec. 401 in force during the war and for six months after its termination; the war had not been terminated by April 1950, and EO 10123 treats the order as still in force, so no earlier statutory lapse is shown. The one earlier event is EO 9904 (November 13, 1947), which replaced the text of para. 8 (order of succession), so the original para. 8 ended on that date. EO 10123 (15 FR 2265) then revoked EO 9635 and EO 9904 without a stated effective date, so every other paragraph ended on its signing date, April 20, 1950, which is the whole-order end. The National Security Act of 1947 and its 1949 amendments, which reorganized the military establishment, were not read here; no held source (OFR catalog, U.S. Code notes, 1989 Codification table) records that they revoked or replaced any paragraph, which is a limit of this bounded search rather than a finding. Savings: EO 10123 keeps EOs 8984 and 9096 revoked (non-revival), an effect now resting on EO 10123. The OFR catalog and the 1989 Codification table (a lead) list no other amendment.

research_rationale: EO 10440 (March 31, 1953; 18 FR 1823-1824, read in the held govinfo scan) rewrote Civil Service Rule VI (secs. 6.1-6.6, creating Schedule C) and in sec. 2 directed the Commission to reclassify existing Schedule A and B positions, keeping them in place until it acted. Earlier events: EO 10463 (June 25, 1953) replaced sec. 6.4, so the original sec. 6.4 ended that day. The other Rule VI sections continued until EO 10577 sec. 301 revoked EO 10440 by name, effective (sec. 401) on the first Sunday after the sixtieth day after November 22, 1954, i.e. January 23, 1955, which is therefore the whole-order end (no later-ending clause exists). Sec. 2 is a transitional direction that was spent once the Commission had reclassified every listed position; the date that happened is not in the held sources, so its first end is left open rather than set to the revocation date. Savings: EO 10577's proviso carried the schedule listings into the new rules.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 11515 sec. 6 provides that 'such actions as may be necessary to wind up any outstanding affairs of the bodies terminated by this order shall be carried out by the Bureau of the Budget' or agencies its Director designates. The Board's residual affairs were thus transferred for winding up only; no function, right or obligation of the Board was continued. EO 10898 itself has no savings provision, and sec. 4 made the Board advisory, without control over any agency, so no agency action depended on it.

research_rationale: EO 10898 (December 2, 1960; 25 FR 12429, read in the held govinfo scan) established the Interdepartmental Highway Safety Board of cabinet officers (sec. 1), gave it coordinating and study functions (sec. 2), provided agency assistance (sec. 3), made it advisory only (sec. 4) and required reports (sec. 5). It has no term of its own. Earlier clause-level ends: EO 10986 (January 12, 1962) substituted a new sec. 1(b), so the original membership list ended then; EO 11382 sec. 8 (November 28, 1967) struck all of sec. 1(b) as amended and changed the quorum in sec. 1(d) from three to four, so the original quorum rule ended then. EO 11382 sec. 16(3) also revoked EO 10858, which sec. 4 cites for the President's Committee for Traffic Safety; this is recorded as a later event on sec. 4, but the section's main rule (Board advisory only) continued. EO 11515 (March 13, 1970) terminated the Board and revoked EO 10898 and EO 10986 without a stated effective date, so the remaining clauses ended on March 13, 1970, the whole-order end. The Board consisted of federal officials and ended before the Federal Advisory Committee Act (1972) existed, so no statutory termination applies.

research_rationale: EO 11152 (April 15, 1964; 29 FR 5271-5272, read in the held govinfo scan) established the President's Committee on Manpower of cabinet and agency heads to assist the Secretary of Labor under the Manpower Development and Training Act (secs. 1-4). It has no term or condition of its own, no amendment is recorded (OFR catalog; 1989 Codification table, a lead), and it ended before the Federal Advisory Committee Act (1972) existed, so no statutory termination applies. EO 11515 sec. 3 terminated the Committee and revoked EO 11152 without a stated effective date, so every clause ended on March 13, 1970. Winding up went to the Bureau of the Budget (sec. 6).

research_rationale: EO 11126 (November 1, 1963; 28 FR 11717-11718, read in the held govinfo scan) set up an Interdepartmental Committee on the Status of Women of cabinet officers (Part I) and a Citizens' Advisory Council on the Status of Women (Part II), with support provisions (Part III). It has no term of its own. Clause-level history: EO 11221 (May 6, 1965) substituted new texts for secs. 101(a), 103 and 201, so the original texts ended then. The Council was an advisory committee in existence on January 5, 1973 and would have expired under sec. 14(a)(1) of the Federal Advisory Committee Act on January 5, 1975, but EO 11827 (signed January 4, 1975) continued it to January 5, 1977 and EO 11948 (effective December 31, 1976) to December 31, 1978, so there was no statutory lapse. EO 12007 (August 22, 1977) terminated the Council and revoked sec. 102(5) and Part II and rewrote sec. 103 and the second sentence of sec. 301, so those clauses ended then. The Committee clauses (federal officials, outside the Act) continued until EO 12050 sec. 8 revoked EO 11126 as amended, signed April 4, 1978 with no other effective date stated: that is the whole-order end. None of these orders contains a savings clause.

unresolved_material_gaps: Public Law 94-167 (89 Stat. 1003), the statute under which the Commission operated after 1975, is not held and was not read; its duration and termination terms decide when the Commission clauses (secs. 1(a), 1(c), 1(d), 2(a)-(g), 3) ended (on or before April 4, 1978).
Sec. 4 interdepartmental task force for International Women's Year: date on which it was spent or ended not established (no later than April 4, 1978, EO 12050).
whole_order_end not set: depends on the two items above; EO 12050 sec. 8 (signed April 4, 1978) is the latest possible date, not a confirmed first end.
savings_residuals not closed: EO 12050 has no savings clause, but whether Public Law 94-167 preserved or transferred any Commission function or report duty has not been read.
research_rationale: EO 11832 (January 9, 1975; 40 FR 2415-2417, read in the held govinfo scan) established the National Commission on the Observance of International Women's Year, 1975 (secs. 1-3) and an interdepartmental task force (sec. 4). Exact clause-level ends found: EO 11889 (November 25, 1975) replaced the original sec. 2(h), which had ended the Commission's work with 1975; EO 11979 (March 28, 1977) replaced the original sec. 1(b) membership rule (further amended by EO 11980). The other clauses are certainly terminated by the cutoff, since EO 12050 sec. 8 revoked EO 11832 as amended on April 4, 1978, but that revocation may be a clean-up. Under EO 11889 the Commission was to end after a final report due within thirty days after June 30, 1976. EO 11979 shows it was still operating in 1977 'in accord with Section 2' of Public Law 94-167, which directed it to organize the National Women's Conference, and the Commission was set up after the Federal Advisory Committee Act took effect, so sec. 14(a)(2) of that Act also bears on its duration. Without reading Public Law 94-167, which states how long the Commission lasted and when it ended, the first ends of the Commission and task-force clauses, the whole-order end and the savings question cannot be fixed honestly; they are left open.

research_rationale: EO 11534 (June 4, 1970; 35 FR 8865, read in the held govinfo scan) created a National Council on Organized Crime of eighteen named federal officials to formulate a national strategy against organized crime. It has no term, report deadline or condition, and no amendment is recorded (OFR catalog; 1989 Codification table, a lead). EO 12110 sec. 1-103(c) lists it among orders 'that established committees which have terminated or whose work is completed'. That recital gives no date and is not itself a legal act ending the Council earlier; the order's own terms set no end, and the Council, composed wholly of full-time federal officers, was outside the termination rule of sec. 14 of the Federal Advisory Committee Act (the continuance orders EO 11827 and EO 11948 accordingly do not list it). The legal first end of every clause is therefore the revocation, effective December 31, 1978 under sec. 1-105. Changes in some members' offices (for example the Post Office Department and the Bureau of Narcotics and Dangerous Drugs were later reorganized) altered who sat on the Council but did not end it; they were not separately researched.

various national labor organizations and contractor associations in  
the construction industry. Alternate members also may be designated.

research_rationale: EO 11482 (September 22, 1969; 34 FR 14723-14725, read in the held govinfo scan) created a tripartite Construction Industry Collective Bargaining Commission with study, recommendation, dispute-intercession, rule-making and reporting functions (secs. 1-9). Clause inventory from the official scan, with each provision quoted from one page. EO 12110 sec. 1-103(a) revoked it effective December 31, 1978 (sec. 1-105) as one whose committee had 'terminated' or whose work was 'completed', so the revocation is likely a clean-up after an earlier end. The candidate earlier end is statutory: under Federal Advisory Committee Act sec. 14(a)(1), advisory committees in existence on January 5, 1973 terminated on January 5, 1975 unless renewed, and EO 11827 sec. 4 says the same of presidential committees it did not continue; EO 11827 did not continue this Commission. Whether the Act reached this body, which mediated and intervened in disputes as well as advising, is a legal question left open, so first ends are not asserted. The CONFLICT (29 CFR part 901 still cites the order) is left open because the eCFR text is not on this machine.

unresolved_material_gaps: First end of every clause not established. The Committee (ten labor and ten management members appointed by the President) was created April 1, 1975, after the Federal Advisory Committee Act took effect; under its sec. 14(a)(2) (held 86 Stat. 776) such a committee terminates not later than two years after establishment unless renewed. EO 11948 (effective 1976-12-31), the general continuance order, did not renew it, and EO 12110 sec. 1-103(b) describes it as terminated or its work completed. Whether the Act applied and whether any separate renewal was made has not been established, so the expiry date (about April 1, 1977) is not asserted.

research_rationale: EO 11849 (April 1, 1975; 40 FR 14887-14888, read in the held govinfo scan) created the Collective Bargaining Committee in Construction (secs. 1-6). The order has no term of its own. EO 12110 sec. 1-103(b) revoked it effective December 31, 1978 as one whose committee had 'terminated' or whose work was 'completed', which signals an earlier end. The likely earlier end is the two-year limit of Federal Advisory Committee Act sec. 14(a)(2), since the general continuance order of December 1976 (EO 11948) did not renew it. Because the Act's application and the absence of any other renewal are not proven from held sources, first ends and the whole-order end are left open. Savings: none found. The U.S. Code note (29 U.S.C. 171 note) and the eCFR hits are historical and report the revocation; no CONFLICT is open.

unresolved_material_gaps: Actual date of submission of the Committee's report (due no later than June 11, 1977 under EO 11982) and any presidential extension under sec. 3(b) not established; the Committee terminated thirty days after submission unless extended, so the first end of the clauses tied to its existence cannot be dated. A deadline does not prove the report date. EO 12110 (effective 1978-12-31) describes the Committee as terminated or its work completed.
whole_order_end not set until the report and extension question is resolved (latest possible date 1978-12-31).
research_rationale: EO 11971 (February 11, 1977; 42 FR 9155-9156, read in the held govinfo scan) created a temporary Committee on Selection of the Director of the FBI (secs. 1-7). Sec. 3(b) makes it terminate thirty days after it submits its report unless the President extends it. EO 11982 (April 29, 1977) replaced the original sec. 3(a), so that clause's first end is exact. All other clauses depended on the Committee's existence, which ended under the order's own terms at a date not recorded in held sources, or, if extended, no later than EO 12110's revocation effective December 31, 1978. EO 12110 itself describes the Committee as terminated or its work completed. Those first ends and the whole-order end are left open rather than inferred from the June 11, 1977 deadline. Savings: none found.

military compensation issues, specifically addressing the following issues:

military compensation? If so, what should the standards be? What elements of com­
pensation should be based on such standards?

cial and incentive pays) and what are the appropriate criteria for using them?

effective in achieving these purposes? What changes are appropriate?
(5) Should the unique characteristics of military service be reflected in the com­
pensation system, and, if so, how?

unresolved_material_gaps: Exact first end of the clauses that lasted until the revocation not established: EO 9687 (signed January 26, 1946; 11 FR 1033) revoked the order but 'shall become effective with respect to any agency concerned as of the close of its pay period terminating or current on January 31, 1946'. The effective date therefore differs by agency (January 31, 1946, or the later close of a pay period current on that day), so no single exact date can be asserted for those clauses or for the whole order.

EO 9449 (effective July 1, 1944) made no losses payable to most War and Navy Department personnel and by its sec. 2 amended 'accordingly' every conflicting provision of EO 7972 as amended; how far that implied amendment ended the clauses marked with the EO 9449 later event has not been delimited.

savings_residuals not closed: EO 9687 has no savings clause; whether claims for currency-appreciation losses that accrued before each agency's effective date remained payable (accrued rights under the Act of March 26, 1934, as amended) has not been established.
research_rationale: EO 7972 (September 15, 1938; 3 FR 2249-2252, read in the held govinfo scan) prescribed regulations for paying currency-appreciation losses of officers, enlisted men and employees serving abroad (secs. 1-7), with a table of basic rates in sec. 4. It was amended by EOs 8018 (new sec. 3(h)), 8261 (additions to sec. 1(b); new sec. 2(b)), 8269 (complete new rate table, effective December 1, 1939), 8800, 9057 and 9261 (table entries) and 9449 (new sec. 2(b) and conflict amendment, effective July 1, 1944), and was revoked with all of them by EO 9687. Exact clause-level ends: the original sec. 2(b) ended September 21, 1939 (EO 8261) and the original rate table December 1, 1939 (EO 8269). The other clauses lasted until EO 9687, whose effective date is set agency by agency at the close of the pay period terminating or current on January 31, 1946, so no single exact date can be asserted. EO 9449's conflict amendment also cut back several clauses for War and Navy personnel from July 1, 1944, to an extent not delimited here. Sec. 7's supersession of EO 6928 was a one-time disposition; EO 9687 does not say whether its revocation revives earlier orders, and none was found to have been revived. The first ends, whole-order end and savings are left open.

unresolved_material_gaps: Exact first end of the clauses that lasted until the revocation not established: EO 9687 (signed January 26, 1946; 11 FR 1033) revoked the order but 'shall become effective with respect to any agency concerned as of the close of its pay period terminating or current on January 31, 1946'. The effective date therefore differs by agency (January 31, 1946, or the later close of a pay period current on that day), so no single exact date can be asserted for those clauses or for the whole order.

EO 9449 (effective July 1, 1944) made no losses payable to most War and Navy Department personnel and by its sec. 2 amended 'accordingly' every conflicting provision of EO 7972 as amended; how far that implied amendment ended the clauses marked with the EO 9449 later event has not been delimited.

savings_residuals not closed: EO 9687 has no savings clause; whether claims for currency-appreciation losses that accrued before each agency's effective date remained payable (accrued rights under the Act of March 26, 1934, as amended) has not been established.
research_rationale: EO 8018 (December 2, 1938; 3 FR 2861, read in the held govinfo scan) has one operative provision: it adds sec. 3(h) to EO 7972 (computation of losses by Navy and Marine Corps disbursing officers at the disbursing officer's average cost rate, retroactive to April 1, 1934 for earlier credits, and no loss payable once the currency has fallen to the basic rate). No later order replaced sec. 3(h). EO 9449 (effective July 1, 1944) made no losses payable to most Navy personnel and amended conflicting provisions 'accordingly', which cut back this paragraph to an extent not delimited here. EO 9687 revoked EO 8018 by name, effective agency by agency at the close of the pay period terminating or current on January 31, 1946, so no exact first end can be asserted. Savings are left open.

Title 3— Executive Order 12720 of July 16, 1990
The President President’s Council on Rural America
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and laws of the 
United States of America, and in order to establish, in accordance with the 
provisions of the Federal Advisory Committee Act, as amended (5 U.S.C.  
App.), an advisory council on the rural economic development policy of the 
United States, it is hereby ordered as follows:
Section 1. E s ta b lis h m e n t, (a) There is established the President's Council on 
Rural America (“Council”). The Council shall be composed of not more than 
twenty (20) members to be appointed by the President.
(b) The President shall appoint a Chairman and Vice Chairman from among 
the members of the Council.
Sec. 2. F u n ctio n s, (a} The Council shall advise the President and the Economic 
Policy Council on how the Federal Government can improve its rural econom­
ic development policy.
(b) In the performance of its advisory duties, the Council shall conduct such 
continuing reviews and assessments of the Federal Government's rural eco­
nomic development policy as deemed necessary or appropriate by the Coun­
cil.
Sec. 3. A d m in is tr a tio n , (a) The heads of executive agencies shall, to the extent 
permitted by law, provide the Council such information with respect to rural 
economic development policy matters as the Council deems required for the 
purpose of carrying out its functions.
(b) Members of the Council who are not otherwise officers or employee» of the 
Federal Government shall serve without any compensation for their work on 
the Council However, they shall be entitled to travel expenses, including per 
diem in lieu of subsistence, as authorized by law for persons serving intermit­
tently in tiie Government service (5 U.S.C. 5701-5707).
(c) To the extent permitted by law and subject to the availability of appropria­
tions, the Farmers Home Administration shall provide the Council with achnin- 
istrative services, facilities, staff, and other support services necessary for the 
performance of its functions. Funds for the operation of the Council shall be 
provided by the Department of Agriculture.
•(d) Notwithstanding any other Executive order, the functions of the President 
under the Federal Advisory Committee Act, as amended, except that of  
reporting to the Congress, which are applicable to the Council shall be  
performed by the Secretary of Agriculture in accordance with guidelines  
issued by the Administrator of General Services.

Kuwait by Iraq. To provide additional authority to the Department of Defense 
to respond to that threat, and in accordance with section 301 of the National 
Emergencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1631), I hereby order that the emergency construc­
tion authority at 10 U.S.C. 2808 is invoked and made available in accordance 
with its terms to the Secretary of Defense and, at the discretion of the 
Secretary of Defense, to the Secretaries of the military departments.
This order is effective immediately and shall be transmitted to the Congress 
and published in the Federal Register.

Title 3— 
The President 
Executive Order 13350 of July 29, 2004
Termination of Emergency Declared in Executive Order 
12722 With Respect to Iraq and Modification of Executive 
Order 13290, Executive Order 13303, and Executive Order 
13315
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and laws 
of the United States of America, including the International Emergency 
Economic Powers Act (50 U.S.C. 1701 et seq .)(IEEPA), the National Emer-
gencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1601 et seq .)(NEA), section 5 of the United Nations 
Participation Act, as amended (22 U.S.C. 287c)(UNPA), and section 301 
of title 3, United States Code, 
I, GEORGE W. BUSH, President of the United States of America, have 
determined that the situation that gave rise to the declaration of a national 
emergency with respect to Iraq in Executive Order 12722 of August 2, 
1990, has been significantly altered by the removal of the regime of Saddam 
Hussein and other developments. I hereby terminate the national emergency 
declared in Executive Order 12722, revoke that Executive Order and Execu-
tive Order 12724 of August 9, 1990, Executive Order 12734 of November 
14, 1990, Executive Order 12743 of January 18, 1991, Executive Order 12751 
of February 14, 1991, and Executive Order 12817 of October 21, 1992, 
that are based on that national emergency. I hereby amend Executive Order 
13290 of March 20, 2003, so that the authorities therein remain in effect 
based on the national emergency I declared in Executive Order 13303 of 
May 22, 2003, and expanded in Executive Order 13315 of August 28, 2003. 
At the same time, and in order to take additional steps to deal with the 
national emergency that I declared in Executive Order 13303, and expanded 
in Executive Order 13315, with respect to the unusual and extraordinary 
threat to the national security and foreign policy of the United States posed 
by obstacles to the orderly reconstruction of Iraq, the restoration and mainte-
nance of peace and security in that country, and the development of political, 
administrative and economic institutions in Iraq, I hereby order: 
Section 1. Pursuant to section 202(a) of the NEA (50 U.S.C. 1622(a)), termi-
nation of the national emergency declared in Executive Order 12722 shall 
not affect any action taken or proceeding pending but not finally concluded 
or determined as of the effective date of this order, any action or proceeding 
based on any act committed prior to such date, or any rights or duties 
that matured or penalties that were incurred prior to such date. Pursuant 
to section 207(a) of IEEPA (50 U.S.C. 1706(a)), and subject to such regulations, 
orders, directives, or licenses as may be issued pursuant to this order, 
I hereby determine that the continuation of prohibitions with regard to 
transactions involving property blocked pursuant to Executive Orders 12722 
or 12724 that continues to be blocked as of the effective date of this order 
is necessary on account of claims involving Iraq. 
Sec. 2. The Annex to Executive Order 13315 is replaced and superseded 
in its entirety by the Annex to this order. 
Sec. 3. I hereby amend Executive Order 13290 by removing ‘‘the national 
emergency declared in Executive Order 12722 of August 2, 1990’’ and replac-
ing it with ‘‘the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13303 
of March 20, 2003, and expanded in Executive Order 13315 of August 
28, 2003’’.

Sec. 4. Unless licensed or otherwise authorized pursuant to this order or 
otherwise consistent with U.S. law, the trade in or transfer of ownership 
or possession of Iraqi cultural property or other items of archeological, 
historical, cultural, rare scientific, and religious importance that were illegally 
removed, or for which a reasonable suspicion exists that they were illegally 
removed, from the Iraq National Museum, the National Library, and other 
locations in Iraq since August 6, 1990, is prohibited. 
Sec. 5. I hereby determine that the making of donations of the type specified 
in section 203(b)(2) of IEEPA (50 U.S.C. 1702(b)(2)) by or to persons deter-
mined to be subject to the sanctions imposed by Executive Order 13315 
or by this order would seriously impair my ability to deal with the national 
emergency declared in Executive Order 13303, and expanded by Executive 
Order 13315, or would endanger the Armed Forces of the United States 
that are engaged in hostilities, and I hereby prohibit such donations as 
provided in section 1 of Executive Order 13315 as amended by this order. 
Sec. 6. For those persons listed in the Annex to this order or determined 
to be subject to Executive Order 13315 or this order who might have a 
constitutional presence in the United States, I find that because of the 
ability to transfer funds or other assets instantaneously, prior notice to 
such persons of measures to be taken pursuant to this order would render 
these measures ineffectual. I therefore determine that for these measures 
to be effective in addressing the national emergency declared in Executive 
Order 13303, and expanded by Executive Order 13315, there need be no 
prior notice of a listing or determination made pursuant to Executive Order 
13315 or this order. 
Sec. 7. The Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with the Secretary 
of State, is hereby authorized to take such actions, including the promulgation 
of rules and regulations, and to employ all powers granted to the President 
by IEEPA and UNPA as may be necessary to carry out the purposes of 
this order. The Secretary of the Treasury may redelegate any of these func-
tions to other officers and agencies of the United States Government con-
sistent with applicable law. All agencies of the United States Government 
are hereby directed to take all appropriate measures within their authority 
to carry out the provisions of this order. 
Sec. 8. The Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with the Secretary 
of State, is authorized to determine subsequent to the issuance of the order, 
that circumstances no longer warrant the inclusion of a person in the Annex 
to this order and that such person is therefore no longer covered within 
the scope of the order. 
Sec. 9. This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or 
benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any 
party against the United States, its departments, agencies, instrumentalities, 
or entities, officers or employees, or any other person.

Title 3— 
The President 
Executive Order 13350 of July 29, 2004
Termination of Emergency Declared in Executive Order 
12722 With Respect to Iraq and Modification of Executive 
Order 13290, Executive Order 13303, and Executive Order 
13315
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and laws 
of the United States of America, including the International Emergency 
Economic Powers Act (50 U.S.C. 1701 et seq .)(IEEPA), the National Emer-
gencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1601 et seq .)(NEA), section 5 of the United Nations 
Participation Act, as amended (22 U.S.C. 287c)(UNPA), and section 301 
of title 3, United States Code, 
I, GEORGE W. BUSH, President of the United States of America, have 
determined that the situation that gave rise to the declaration of a national 
emergency with respect to Iraq in Executive Order 12722 of August 2, 
1990, has been significantly altered by the removal of the regime of Saddam 
Hussein and other developments. I hereby terminate the national emergency 
declared in Executive Order 12722, revoke that Executive Order and Execu-
tive Order 12724 of August 9, 1990, Executive Order 12734 of November 
14, 1990, Executive Order 12743 of January 18, 1991, Executive Order 12751 
of February 14, 1991, and Executive Order 12817 of October 21, 1992, 
that are based on that national emergency. I hereby amend Executive Order 
13290 of March 20, 2003, so that the authorities therein remain in effect 
based on the national emergency I declared in Executive Order 13303 of 
May 22, 2003, and expanded in Executive Order 13315 of August 28, 2003. 
At the same time, and in order to take additional steps to deal with the 
national emergency that I declared in Executive Order 13303, and expanded 
in Executive Order 13315, with respect to the unusual and extraordinary 
threat to the national security and foreign policy of the United States posed 
by obstacles to the orderly reconstruction of Iraq, the restoration and mainte-
nance of peace and security in that country, and the development of political, 
administrative and economic institutions in Iraq, I hereby order: 
Section 1. Pursuant to section 202(a) of the NEA (50 U.S.C. 1622(a)), termi-
nation of the national emergency declared in Executive Order 12722 shall 
not affect any action taken or proceeding pending but not finally concluded 
or determined as of the effective date of this order, any action or proceeding 
based on any act committed prior to such date, or any rights or duties 
that matured or penalties that were incurred prior to such date. Pursuant 
to section 207(a) of IEEPA (50 U.S.C. 1706(a)), and subject to such regulations, 
orders, directives, or licenses as may be issued pursuant to this order, 
I hereby determine that the continuation of prohibitions with regard to 
transactions involving property blocked pursuant to Executive Orders 12722 
or 12724 that continues to be blocked as of the effective date of this order 
is necessary on account of claims involving Iraq. 
Sec. 2. The Annex to Executive Order 13315 is replaced and superseded 
in its entirety by the Annex to this order. 
Sec. 3. I hereby amend Executive Order 13290 by removing ‘‘the national

I hereby terminate the national emergency 
declared in Executive Order 12722, revoke that Executive Order and Execu-
tive Order 12724 of August 9, 1990, Executive Order 12734 of November 
14, 1990, Executive Order 12743 of January 18, 1991, Executive Order 12751 
of February 14, 1991, and Executive Order 12817 of October 21, 1992, 
that are based on that national emergency.
